# Vancouver Daily News
> **Nine hundred fourteen dollars is what the average home would pay Metro Vancouver if Friday's budget vote holds.**

**What You Need to Know:** Metro Vancouver's outgoing board still plans to vote Friday on a 2027 budget that would lift the average household's regional services bill to $914 from $897. Surrey mayor-elect Doug McCallum and New Westminster mayor-elect Daniel Fontaine want that meeting cancelled until the new board is in place. A Metro Vancouver spokesperson says the Friday vote stays on so member cities can build their own budgets.

### The Closer Look
**Dan Fumano: In poignant final council meeting, Vancouver Mayor Ken Sim and most of his party say goodbye and good luck: Vancouver Sun**
Ken Sim presided Tuesday over his last Vancouver city council meeting, the only public session between the October 17 election that defeated him and ABC and the November 2 swearing-in of the new council.

Partway through, he dropped the titles he had used for four years. Instead of Coun. Kirby-Yung, Coun. Dominato and Coun. Fry, he said Sarah, Lisa and Pete. Vancouver Sun columnist Dan Fumano wrote that the change did not read as disrespect, but as warmth toward colleagues his party had campaigned against, sometimes aggressively.

The term opened on a different note. After ABC's 2022 landslide, Sim's party gave some board roles to councillors from outside the team and talked about being post-partisan. By the halfway point, Sim had stripped non-ABC councillors of those extra roles and the pay that came with them. In 2023, 2024 and 2025, politicians elected with ABC resigned from caucus or were ejected after splits over abolishing the elected park board, halting the municipal ethics watchdog's work, and freezing supportive housing construction.

When the campaign began in September, Sim was party to two defamation lawsuits that are still going. He is the plaintiff suing former chief of staff Kareem Allam, who ran against him for mayor. He is a defendant in a suit filed by Coun. Sean Orr.

Before Tuesday's meeting, Sim embraced Orr, who was re-elected with three new councillors from COPE. Asked about that chat, Sim said, "You know, bygones be bygones," and that Orr had stepped up to serve even where their politics differ.

Outgoing councillors then addressed the room. ABC's Lisa Dominato, Sarah Kirby-Yung, Lenny Zhou and Peter Meiszner, all defeated for a second term, and Rebecca Bligh, elected with ABC in 2022 and a mayoral candidate this year against Sim, thanked staff and voters and wished their successors well. Brian Montague, who did not seek re-election, attended and did not speak.

Sim spoke last. He thanked his family, joked, and paraphrased Dickens to his colleagues: it had been the best of times, and sometimes not the best of times, and he was not going to say the worst of times. He said that on his deathbed he would look back on being mayor as the most meaningful thing he had been involved in. The new council is sworn in November 2. Fumano's column notes that Pete Fry, who unseated Sim, will be Vancouver's first Green mayor. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/opinion/columnists/vancouver-mayor-ken-sim-abc-party-final-council-meeting) Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/player/play/video/9.7399054)

### Both Sides: Metro Vancouver's Friday budget vote
Friday, Metro Vancouver's board meets to work through a 1,190-page agenda and to approve the 2027 budget and five-year financial plan. The board is mayors and councillors from 21 municipalities, each with a weighted vote by the size of their city. The proposed budget calls for nearly $1.7 billion in operating spending, a 7.4 per cent increase from this year, and $2 billion in planned capital spending. The average household's bill for regional water, sewer, garbage and parks is projected to rise to $914 a year from $897.

Surrey mayor-elect Doug McCallum says Friday's October 30 meeting should be cancelled until the new mayors are sworn in. He says that on October 17, voters in 13 of the region's 21 municipalities chose a new mayor, including Vancouver, Surrey, Richmond, Coquitlam, Delta and both Langleys, and that an outgoing board should not set what every household pays. His strongest reason is time and accountability: the board has until next March to adopt its financial plan, so waiting for the November 27 regular meeting should not be a problem. If one item truly cannot wait four weeks, he says, deal with that item and leave the rest. He has asked board chair Mike Hurley and the directors to cancel.

New Westminster mayor-elect Daniel Fontaine says he fully supports that request. He says about two-thirds of the 41 directors were defeated, resigned or did not run again, and that ratifying a significant budget in the dying days of this board is incomprehensible. His case is that people who will not face the voters for these decisions should not lock in a plan the next board may have to manage for four years. He says Metro Vancouver is not under a statutory deadline to approve the budget Friday. He also plans to push an accountability charter, already backed by West Vancouver's mayor-elect Kirk LaPointe and White Rock's mayor-elect Chris Shields, including a full review of cost overruns at the North Shore wastewater treatment plant.

A Metro Vancouver spokesperson said Monday the 2027 budget will be considered and voted on this Friday. The reason given is practical: an October decision gives member jurisdictions time to prepare their own financial plans and to meet legislative requirements for when budgets should be established. The spokesperson said board meetings fall on the last Friday of every month regardless of the election cycle. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/metro-vancouver-rejects-surrey-doug-mccallum-cancel-meeting)

# Vancouver Daily News
> **BC Ferries removes CEO Nicolas Jimenez and launches a review of service and demand.**

**What You Need to Know:** BC Ferries has removed chief executive Nicolas Jimenez and launched a review of service and demand. Brian Anderson, vice-president of strategy and planning, is interim CEO effective immediately, while chief financial officer Dallyn Willis leads that review and a permanent search follows it. Jimenez took the job in 2023 after leaving ICBC, where he worked with then-Attorney General David Eby on no-fault insurance.

### Top Stories
**Nicolas Jimenez out as B.C. Ferries CEO, review launched: CBC British Columbia**
Nicolas Jimenez is out as chief executive of BC Ferries, and the board has launched a review. Daily Hive reported the departure as sudden. Brian Anderson, vice-president of strategy and planning, is interim CEO effective immediately. Executive vice-president and chief financial officer Dallyn Willis will lead a review aimed at improving service and meeting growing demand, with the board overseeing it. A formal search for a permanent CEO follows that review. Jimenez took over in 2023 after leaving ICBC, where he had worked closely with then-Attorney General David Eby on the transition to no-fault insurance. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/nicolas-jimenez-out-as-b-c-ferries-ceo-review-launched-9.7396867?cmp=rss) Source: [dailyhive.com](https://dailyhive.com/vancouver/hullo-ferries-new-ceo-louisa-bell)

**B.C. election sets record for lowest voter turnout: Global BC**
Elections BC’s preliminary figures show 48 percent of eligible voters cast a ballot, fewer than half, and about 10 percentage points below the 2024 provincial election. Stewart Prest, a political science lecturer at UBC, told Global News, “This is Mr. Eby’s low-turnout election to own, and this is going to be part of his legacy.” The NDP received more than 270,000 fewer votes than in 2024. The Conservatives received about 49,000 fewer. Prest said the early call looked politically opportunistic to some previous NDP supporters, and that the party did not present a positive vision on housing affordability and jobs. He said some Conservative voters, asked back to the polls two years after the last election, were motivated to send the governing party a message. Prest said people are more likely to vote when they believe the vote matters and when governments deliver on housing and jobs. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12120927/bc-election-record-lowest-voter-turnout/)

**Victoria backs amalgamation, but Saanich voters reject becoming a single larger city with B.C.'s capital: Daily Hive Vancouver**
Saanich voters rejected becoming one municipality with Victoria, so the non-binding idea does not have the yes from both communities that Saanich said was required before any further work. In Saanich, 24,663 votes, 68 percent, were against, and 11,626, 32 percent, were in favour. In Victoria, 17,523 votes, 62 percent, were in favour, and 10,890, 38 percent, were against, among 28,413 responses. Both municipalities asked the same question on October 17, 2026: “Do you support Saanich and Victoria becoming one municipality?” Saanich had said a no in either community meant no further amalgamation work. The outgoing BC NDP government had said that even a yes in both places would not merge them: more information on costs, transition and services, plus consultation with area First Nations, would be needed before a binding referendum could be considered. In 2018, voters in both communities supported funding a citizens’ assembly. That assembly of 48 randomly selected residents recommended a merger in 2025, and its final report was presented that July. Source: [dailyhive.com](https://dailyhive.com/vancouver/victoria-saanich-october-2026-amalgamation-plebiscite-election-results)

**Uniqlo to move into old Nordstrom building in downtown Vancouver: Global BC**
Uniqlo said it will open a flagship in the former Nordstrom building at Pacific Centre early next year, in the same year as the tenth anniversary of its first B.C. store, at Metrotown in Burnaby. Nordstrom closed in 2023. Last year the 230,000-square-foot space was slated to be split into four units. Simons and Aritzia are taking two of those quadrants. After Uniqlo takes the third, one unit remains vacant. Nordstrom had been there since 2015. Eaton’s and Sears had left the same location before that. Aritzia said its store will span four levels and include a dining concept it described as casual yet elevated. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12121819/uniqlo-move-nordstrom-building-downtown-vancouver/)

**Vancouver International Airport records its busiest month ever with over 2.8 million passengers: Daily Hive Vancouver**
August 2026 was the first month in Vancouver International Airport’s history to reach and pass 2.8 million passengers, arrivals and departures combined. Daily Hive, using YVR’s latest official statistics, put the August total at 2.815 million. That beat July 2026, itself a record at 2.73 million, by about 83,000 passengers. Before this summer, the busiest month had been August 2018, at 2.71 million.

Compared with August 2025, when YVR recorded 2.65 million passengers, August 2026 was higher by about 168,000, or 6.3 percent. July and August together brought nearly 5.55 million passengers through the airport. WestJet labour disruptions in late July and early August affected both months. August alone averaged about 90,800 passengers a day. September’s final figures are due next month.

Domestic flights were the largest share of August traffic and a large part of the increase in raw numbers, from 1.33 million in August 2025 to 1.45 million, almost 119,000 more passengers, or 8.9 percent. International volumes outside the United States reached over 727,000, up 12.7 percent from about 645,000 in August 2025. Within that, Asia-Pacific routes accounted for about 441,000 passengers, up 18.6 percent. YVR has told Daily Hive it has seen a resurgence in volumes from Mainland China since last year, which it links to the strength of that market. European routes recorded another 240,000 passengers, up 5.2 percent from the same month in 2025.

U.S. transborder volumes moved the other way. They fell to about 635,000 in August 2026, from 668,000 in August 2025, a decline of more than 33,000 passengers, or about five percent. In August 2024, before the re-election of U.S. president Donald Trump, YVR saw 700,000 passengers on U.S. routes. For well over a year, some airlines have reduced frequencies or suspended Canada-U.S. routes and shifted capacity to other domestic and international flying. Air Canada confirmed last week that two seasonal routes linking YVR with Nashville and Raleigh will not return for summer 2027 as previously scheduled.

July’s volumes were driven in part by visitation for the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Growth in July and August was also supported by tourism demand, including a cruise season that brought 1.4 million passengers through the Canada Place terminal. August is typically one of YVR’s busiest months, with summer trips and students heading back for school. Over the first eight months of 2026, YVR recorded 18.92 million passengers, up 4.1 percent from 18.18 million in the same stretch of 2025, and the highest January-to-August total the airport has recorded. The full-year record is 26.9 million passengers in 2025. Daily Hive noted that if the rest of 2026 holds this pace, the annual total could exceed that mark. Source: [dailyhive.com](https://dailyhive.com/vancouver/vancouver-international-airport-yvr-summer-2026-passenger-statistics-record)

### Both Sides: Repealing DRIPA
The B.C. Conservative government-elect says it will repeal the Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act. The Union of B.C. Indian Chiefs says the law should stay and be used, not torn up. The act passed unanimously in the legislature in 2019. Premier-designate Lorne Doerkson said the day after the election that his party is committed to repealing it.

Doerkson’s case is that the law has not solved the conflicts it was meant to settle. He said, “The reality is it hasn’t solved anything.” He pointed to court fights over docks at Pender Harbour and over mining opportunities, and said the province needs to “work together for the betterment of all people in British Columbia.”

Grand Chief Stewart Phillip, president of the Union of British Columbia Indian Chiefs, calls DRIPA the roadmap to reconciliation and the way to recognize inherent title and rights. He said the chiefs will not stand idly by if the government-elect rips it up, and he called that “a declaration of war.” He framed the choice as whether British Columbia becomes “a war zone” or keeps doing “the challenging work of reconciliation.” The Union of B.C. Indian Chiefs urges the new government to use the act as the framework for that work rather than repeal it.

Doerkson said his party is contemplating a shortened fall session, so the repeal is not likely to reach the legislature until spring. # Vancouver Daily News
> **A thirty-two-thousand-dollar basic exemption is the first bill Lorne Doerkson wants for B.C. taxpayers.**

**What You Need to Know:** Premier-designate Lorne Doerkson says his first bill will raise the basic personal exemption to $32,000, so earnings up to that amount are not taxed. A day after the Conservative win, he also left a fall sitting open, named a transition chair, and set a day-one review of a deficit he put at nearly $14 billion. Elsewhere, more than 1,200 workers are off the job at Highland Valley Copper, and about 150 North Vancouver grads spent hours stuck on a party boat in Burrard Inlet.

### Top Stories
**B.C. premier-designate Lorne Doerkson hints at a fall legislative session: Vancouver Sun**
A day after becoming premier-designate, Lorne Doerkson told reporters at the JW Marriott Parq Vancouver that he has not ruled out a fall legislative session, and that briefings with the public service begin in the coming days. He said that on day one the government will launch an independent review of the province’s finances before a budget, citing a deficit of nearly $14 billion and eight credit downgrades in three years, and that within the first 100 days it will stand up an expert commission on keeping emergency rooms open and cutting wait times. The Vancouver Sun reported that his first big bill will raise the basic personal exemption to $32,000, and that the change has to be made by January 1 if British Columbians are to see it in the 2027 tax year; Daily Hive reported the cut as about $1,000 a year for nearly every working British Columbian, and quoted him saying, “We said we will not raise your taxes, and we will not.” Daily Hive also reported NDP forecasts of a $13.8 billion deficit for 2026/2027, $12.7 billion for 2027/2028 and $12 billion for 2028/2029, with total provincial debt expected at $180.9 billion by the end of this fiscal year and almost $236 billion before the end of the decade, against about $89 billion when David Eby became premier in late 2022. He appointed Kim Henderson, former deputy minister to Christy Clark and former head of the public service, to chair the transition team; Daily Hive reported she will do it as a volunteer on unpaid leave from Trans Mountain, and that he has spoken with Lieutenant Governor Wendy Cocchia, with a swearing-in later next month. He said he will remain party leader and called the interim-leader rule an administrative detail; Daily Hive reported the party constitution does not let an interim leader run for the permanent job without a two-thirds vote, and that the board pledged during the campaign to pursue that change. He said he still intends to repeal the Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act, wants that as soon as possible and pointed to the spring 2027 session when asked about timing, while saying he will take a meeting with First Nations any day a partnership can grow. He said he wants a call with Prime Minister Mark Carney and Alberta Premier Danielle Smith on the proposed Pacific Link pipeline, called the U.S. trade conflict the province’s biggest economic threat, and said he wants to talk to Carney about expanding $10-a-day daycare, including spaces in private facilities. He reaffirmed a switch back to a 10-lane bridge to replace the George Massey Tunnel, said early site work should continue for now, and said the immersed-tunnel project cannot proceed in its current form; Daily Hive reported the updated tunnel cost at $8.5 billion, up from $4.15 billion, with no environmental assessment certificate and the bidding split into five contracts. He promised a Respect Local Democracy Act to ban provincial and municipal campaigns within 90 days of each other, said he has no plan yet for the Vancouver Whitecaps but wants a conversation, and said he will hold a business summit in Vancouver next summer. As of Sunday morning the Sun reported the Conservatives had won 59 seats and led in five more, the NDP had won 23 and led in four, and the Greens had won two, with 99.75 percent of ballot boxes reporting and a final count on November 6; Daily Hive later reported the Conservatives leading in 63 of 93 ridings, the NDP ahead in 28 and the Greens in two, with the final count scheduled for November 6 to 10. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/bc-premier-designate-lorne-doerkson) Source: [dailyhive.com](https://dailyhive.com/vancouver/lorne-doerkson-bc-premier-elect-conservative-government-priorities)

**More than 1,200 workers walk off job at B.C. copper mine after contract talks fail: CBC British Columbia**
More than 1,200 workers have walked off the job at Highland Valley Copper near Logan Lake after contract talks broke down. Teck says operations are continuing at reduced capacity. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/highland-valley-copper-mine-strike-9.7395643?cmp=rss)

Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/north-vancouver-graduates-party-boat-stuck-9.7395064?cmp=rss)

### City & Province
**Conservatives sweep Surrey as record 15 Punjab-origin candidates win in British Columbia: The New Indian Express**
The New Indian Express reported that a record 15 Indian-origin candidates from Punjab were elected to the B.C. legislature, passing the 2024 high of 14, with 11 Conservatives and four New Democrats. It cited the 2021 census figure that South Asians account for 9.6 percent of British Columbia’s population, and said seven of the 15 were re-elected, including Deputy Premier Niki Sharma in Vancouver-Hastings and Speaker Raj Chauhan in Burnaby-New Westminster. In Surrey, Mandeep Dhaliwal held Surrey North, Garry Purewal took Surrey-Fleetwood from Jagrup Brar, Harj Dhaliwal took Surrey-Newton from Jessie Sunner, Garry Thind took Surrey-Guildford from Garry Begg a week after also winning a Surrey school-trustee seat, Zeeshan Wahla took Surrey City Centre from Amna Shah, and Jessy Sahota won Surrey-Serpentine River. Other Conservative winners named were Monica Mohan in Delta North, Pavneet Singh in Kelowna-Lake Country-Coldstream, Harman Bhangu in Langley-Abbotsford, Jody Toor in Langley-Willowbrook, Steve Kooner in Richmond-Queensborough and Deep Sandhu in Vancouver-Fraserview; other NDP winners named were Ravi Parmar in Langford-Highlands and Rohini Arora in Burnaby East. The paper said the wins followed a Conservative sweep of Surrey, that final counts in early November could still change the tally, and that once confirmed the 15 would be about one-sixth of the legislature. Source: [newindianexpress.com](https://www.newindianexpress.com/world/2026/Oct/26/conservatives-sweep-surrey-as-record-15-punjab-origin-candidates-win-in-british-columbia) Source: [tribuneindia.com](https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/punjab/15-punjabi-origin-candidates-in-canada-win-british-columbia-polls-as-conservatives-sweep-surrey/)

### The Closer Look
**BC NDP party faithful dismayed at impacts of Eby’s snap election: Island Social Trends**
Island Social Trends reported from Victoria that the snap election has put the B.C. NDP back in Official Opposition after nine years leading the province, and that Sunday found party loyalists still sorting a campaign many had not expected. The next election had been scheduled for October 2028, with two years left in the 43rd Parliament. The provincial campaign also overlapped municipal campaigns already underway toward an October 17 civic vote, with the provincial election set for October 24.

Bowinn Ma, re-elected in North Vancouver-Lonsdale, defended the call on election night and repeated David Eby’s point from the trail: votes to pass legislation had to be cobbled together from MLAs who were in hospital, including for maternity or cancer. Adrian Dix, re-elected in Vancouver-Kingsway for a seventh time, told television the other way. “Obviously it was a mistake to call the election,” Dix said. He said the call overwhelmed the campaign, did not let the party’s issues break through, and hurt people’s assessment of the premier, and that the premier took responsibility that night.

Dix, who lost as NDP leader in 2013, said the burden on a leader who loses is enormous, for the candidates, the people and the issues. He recalled that the NDP won only two seats in 2001, nearly won in 2005, and then won in 2017, 2020 and 2024. “We’ll be back, you bet we’ll be back,” he said. He said the party’s job now is a strong Opposition that holds the Conservatives to account, and he described that victory as one “without substance, a clear platform or agenda.” He called the night immensely disappointing and named losses by incumbent Sunita Dhir, hopeful Richard Zussman, and Surrey candidates Amna Shah and Jesse Sunner, whom he called future stars, plus Jagrup Brar and Gary Begg. He said health care and education delivered over nine years are part of what was at stake.

Former Victoria-Swan Lake MLA Rob Fleming, who held the education file under John Horgan from 2005 to 2024, spoke Saturday night at the South Island after-party in downtown Victoria. “It was David Eby’s decision and it was his decision alone to call this snap election,” Fleming told Island Social Trends. He called it a spectacularly poor political calculus, seen as cynical and unwanted beside the municipal elections. He said Kerry-Lynne Findlay resigned on a Sunday and Eby called the election on a Tuesday anyway, after expecting to run against her. Fleming said good candidates and former ministers who lost would probably not send Eby a best-wishes card. He emceed for four who were re-elected: Diana Gibson, Nina Krieger, Grace Lore and Darlene Rotchford. He also said a Green vote produced Conservatives on the south Island, and that he believes Saanich South was lost for Richard Zussman because of a heavy Green vote. Source: [islandsocialtrends.ca](https://islandsocialtrends.ca/bc-ndp-party-faithful-dismayed-at-impacts-of-ebys-snap-election/)

# Vancouver Daily News
> **Sixty-four seats give the Conservatives a majority, and David Eby is resigning as NDP leader.**

**What You Need to Know:** Sixty-four seats give the Conservatives a majority, and David Eby is resigning as NDP leader after Saturday’s snap election. He conceded less than two hours after polls closed, keeps his own Vancouver seat on the projection, and stays premier only until the new government takes over. Elections BC’s final count runs November 6 to 10.

### Top Stories
**David Eby steps down as BC NDP leader after snap election defeat: Philippine Canadian Inquirer**
Conservative interim leader Lorne Doerkson is premier-elect after Saturday’s vote, with the Conservatives leading in 64 of 93 districts to the NDP’s 27 and the Greens’ two. Island Social Trends, citing Elections BC, put the Conservative share at 48.05 per cent, the NDP at 37.38 per cent and the Greens at 10.97 per cent, with preliminary turnout at 48.06 per cent. Eby, who called the election on September 22 from a one-seat majority, nearly two years early, conceded less than two hours after polls closed at 8 p.m. and told supporters in Vancouver, “This is obviously something I do with a very heavy heart. But it is time for new leadership within our party.” He was projected to hold Vancouver-Point Grey, said he had called Doerkson to congratulate him, and remains premier during the transition. The Philippine Canadian Inquirer reported the result puts Doerkson on course to be the first Conservative premier since 1933; a majority needed 47 seats. The Vancouver Sun counted 1,770,371 votes, 47.97 per cent of registered voters, against more than two million and 58.74 per cent in 2024. Green leader Emily Lowan, 26, won Saanich North and the Islands, and Daily Hive quoted her saying the Greens are “the only party who is equipped to stand against the Conservatives and their existence.” Elections BC’s final count is November 6 to 10; Island Social Trends said about 70,000 mail and other ballots could move close races but not who formed government. Source: [canadianinquirer.net](https://canadianinquirer.net/2026/10/25/david-eby-steps-down-as-bc-ndp-leader-after-snap-election-defeat/) Source: [islandsocialtrends.ca](https://islandsocialtrends.ca/bc-conservatives-win-majority-government-eby-resigns/) Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/bc-election-2026-eight-takeaways-results) Source: [dailyhive.com](https://dailyhive.com/vancouver/bc-greens-emily-lowan-election-night-victory-2026-full-speech)

**B.C. Election Results: NDP loses ground in Vancouver, but still holds most of city: Vancouver Sun**
The NDP won eight of 12 Vancouver ridings and lost three it held in 2024: Vancouver-Langara, Vancouver-Fraserview and Vancouver-Yaletown. Vancouver-Quilchena, the only city riding the Conservatives won in 2024, stayed Conservative. Adrian Dix, re-elected in Vancouver-Renfrew for a seventh time, told the Sun that calling the snap election was “Obviously” a mistake, and that he gives Eby “great credit” for taking responsibility. With all polls reporting, Niki Sharma beat Phyllis Tang 9,706 to 4,794. Terry Yung lost Vancouver-Yaletown to Conservative Margareta Dovgal by 844 votes; Dovgal told the Sun her aim was to be a public advocate on safety, which she called abysmal. In Vancouver-Langara, Sunita Dhir lost to Jaime Stein, who took 50.4 per cent. Amanda Burrows won the NDP seat after Joan Phillip, the previous NDP MLA, died last month at 74. The Conservatives dropped candidate Jordan Zheng McIntosh on October 15 after it was alleged he posted remarks about the Holocaust and Hitler. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/bc-election-results-2026-vancouver) Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/bc-election-day-2026-live-results-riding-map)

### City & Province
**Cariboo-Chilcotin MLA Lorne Doerkson wins re-election for third time in a row: Surrey Now-Leader**
Voters in Cariboo-Chilcotin returned Lorne Doerkson for a third term, with 76.9 per cent of the vote as of 10:30 p.m. and 75 of 89 ballot boxes counted. Kathryn Askew of the NDP had about 17.1 per cent and Douglas Gook of the Greens about 6 per cent. Speaking in Victoria, Doerkson thanked volunteers and said a mill running in Quesnel keeps a trucker working in Surrey, and a mine opening in the North keeps a port busy in Delta. He called the province one economy and said serving as premier would be the honour of his lifetime. Surrey Now-Leader reported it is the first time in over a century that an MLA from the Cariboo has been premier. Source: [surreynowleader.com](https://surreynowleader.com/2026/10/24/cariboo-chilcotin-mla-lorne-doerkson-on-track-to-win-re-election-for-third-time-in-a-row/)

### The Closer Look
**ELECTION NIGHT LIVE: B.C. Conservatives capture all 10 seats as blue wave engulfs Surrey: Surrey Now-Leader**
The Conservatives took all 10 Surrey ridings on Saturday, a clean sweep the Vancouver Sun also recorded, in a city where the party had won six of 10 in 2024. The Sun named longtime NDP MLAs who lost: Jagrup Brar in Surrey-Fleetwood, Amna Shah in Surrey-City Centre, Jessie Sunner in Surrey-Newton and Garry Begg in Surrey-Guildford. Surrey Now-Leader reported Conservative Purewal won Surrey-Fleetwood, ousting Brar.

The closest count was Surrey-City Centre. With all 72 ballot boxes in, Zeeshan Wahla had 5,696 votes, 47.5 per cent, to incumbent Amna Shah’s 5,305, 44.2 per cent. The lead changed hands through the night and, at one point, the two were a single vote apart. Shah had beaten Wahla in 2024 only after an Elections BC recount. Oliver Wildfong took 583 votes and Raman Sharma 418.

In Surrey-Newton, Harj Dhaliwal finished with 7,316 votes to Jessie Sunner’s 5,461, ending years of NDP control. Sunner, Minister of Post-Secondary Education and Future Skills, had won the seat in 2024 with 7,924 votes. In Surrey North, incumbent Mandeep Singh Dhaliwal had 7,378 to Sahib Thind’s 4,201 with all 65 boxes counted. In Surrey-Panorama, Bryan Tepper had 8,557 to Jinny Sims’s 4,886 with all 60 boxes in.

Surrey South went to Megan Knight, the former White Rock mayor, with 12,550 votes, 61.4 per cent, to Parik Tahlan’s 4,533 and CentreBC leader Elenore Sturko’s 2,074, after all 82 boxes. Knight told Peace Arch News she thought Eby “didn’t listen to the people,” and that a Conservative government is likely to look into housing edicts resisted in White Rock. Sturko congratulated Knight and said she hoped the new government serves British Columbia well. In Surrey-White Rock, Trevor Halford won again with 14,332 votes, 58.2 per cent, to Darryl Walker’s 7,123. Halford told supporters that some 20,000 B.C. workers had lost their jobs in recent weeks and said, “Tonight, David Eby lost his job.”

Garry Thind won Surrey-Guildford with 7,693 votes to Garry Begg’s 6,230, all 76 boxes counted. A week earlier he had placed second for Surrey school trustee with 43,900 votes, after the September 18 withdrawal deadline had passed and his name stayed on the October 17 civic ballot. He told Surrey Now-Leader he had not yet been sworn in as trustee and that staff were looking for a legal way to avoid a byelection. The Eligibility to Hold Public Office Act, as the paper cited it, disqualifies an MLA from local office and deems the person to have resigned that office on the date of the writ. Thind said people would be happy if taxpayers did not pay for another vote. The Sun said the same Conservative wave also swept Delta and Richmond. Source: [surreynowleader.com](https://surreynowleader.com/2026/10/24/b-c-battleground-election-night-live-in-surrey-white-rock/) Source: [surreynowleader.com](https://surreynowleader.com/2026/10/24/b-c-votes-wahla-wins-surrey-city-centre-for-conservatives-in-rematch-with-ndps-shah/) Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/bc-election-2026-eight-takeaways-results)

**What You Need to Know:** British Columbians are voting today for 93 MLAs in the snap provincial election, with polls open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. Vancouver Police are looking for an 80-year-old man last seen near Columbia Street and West 43rd Avenue, and Coquitlam RCMP want help finding a woman named in a Canada-wide warrant. The B.C. Lions lost 34-10 at BC Place as Winnipeg clinched a playoff spot.

### Top Stories
**Voters head to the polls for B.C. provincial election: CBC British Columbia**
Voters are casting ballots today for 93 MLAs after a snap election called last month. NanaimoNewsNOW reports polls open at 8 a.m. and close at 8 p.m. in the vote NDP Leader David Eby called two years early. He initially said he needed a new mandate for challenges posed by U.S. President Donald Trump. Eby said Friday the election was needed to end frustrations of a “stalled out” legislature where the NDP held a one-seat majority, and that he regretted not making that clearer. The five-week campaign, NanaimoNewsNOW reports, turned on health care, housing, the province’s record deficit and the cost of living. Business in Vancouver reports Eby said, as he wrapped the final day of campaigning, that Saturday’s election will be determined by the large group of people still undecided and sitting at home. The Canadian Press reports Eby called Conservative Leader Lorne Doerkson a “Trojan horse” for Conservative extremists as the campaign wrapped. **RCMP ask public for help locating 43-year-old wanted woman last seen in Coquitlam park: Castanet**
Coquitlam RCMP are asking the public to help find 43-year-old Chelcey Hodder, wanted on a Canada-wide warrant of committal after she failed to return to her facility. Police say she was last seen Friday, October 23, at about 2:30 p.m. in the area of ƛ̓éxətəm Regional Park in Coquitlam. They describe her as a white woman, 5 feet 2 inches (157 cm), about 90 pounds (41 kg), with brown-blonde hair, hazel eyes and a star tattoo on her right wrist, last seen in black pants, black shoes, a black shirt and a black jacket. Cpl. Brett Urano, a B.C. RCMP spokesperson, said any information on her whereabouts could help investigators locate her safely. Police say do not approach her; call police, or the Coquitlam RCMP non-emergency line at 604-945-1550. Source: [castanet.net](https://www.castanet.net/news/BC/635546/RCMP-ask-public-for-help-locating-43-year-old-wanted-woman-last-seen-in-Coquitlam-park)

### City & Province
**Why the BC NDP and Conservatives are making so many election promises to Surrey: Daily Hive Vancouver**
Daily Hive reports that on Thursday, October 22, the BC NDP and the Conservative Party of British Columbia each issued announcements aimed at Surrey ridings. Surrey-named ridings, including Surrey-White Rock, are 10 of 93 provincial districts. Conservative Leader Lorne Doerkson has promised a third Surrey hospital as a women’s and children’s hospital, with an estimated $25 million in a first term for a site, a concept and detailed planning; the platform does not promise the hospital would open in that term. Surrey mayor-elect Doug McCallum and his Safe Surrey Coalition have promised City-owned land on King George Boulevard in Newton for a provincial hospital project. NDP Leader David Eby has promised to work with Surrey on another healthcare facility if the city provides land, and has not identified it as a full-service hospital. The NDP has also promised three more urgent and primary care centres in Surrey, further work at Surrey Memorial Hospital, and a purpose-built SFU medical school building in Surrey City Centre expected to cost $520 million, with construction expected to begin in late 2026 and finish in 2030. Eby has promised legislation for a “Surrey Charter,” similar to the Vancouver Charter. McCallum appeared at a Conservative rally in Surrey on Thursday and endorsed Doerkson’s party. **Winnipeg Blue Bombers clinch CFL playoff spot with 34-10 win over B.C. Lions: Northern Sentinel**

The Lions, already in the playoffs, rested many starters and led 10-3 before starting quarterback Zach Collaros left after a hit from B.C.’s Nathan Cherry. Backup Dru Brown finished 11-for-11 for 185 yards and two touchdowns, to Dorian Singer and Nic Demski. Brady Oliveira scored on runs of 63 and 4 yards. Winnipeg is 9-9, tied with Calgary. If Saskatchewan beats Edmonton on Saturday, Winnipeg finishes fourth in the West and crosses over to play Toronto; if Saskatchewan loses, Winnipeg is third and plays the Lions (10-8) in a Western Semifinal on Halloween at 1:30 p.m. in Vancouver. Kaidon Salter, starting for Nathan Rourke, was 12-for-21 for 177 yards and a 36-yard touchdown to Nate DeMontagnac, that receiver’s first CFL touchdown. Sean Whyte’s 48-yard field goal was the 600th of his CFL career, on his 41st birthday. Chris Oladokun finished 7-for-11 for 48 yards and an interception. ### Both Sides: SkyTrain to Newton
Voters are being asked to weigh a promised SkyTrain extension along King George Boulevard from Surrey City Centre to Newton Town Centre. Daily Hive reports both the Conservative Party of British Columbia and the BC NDP announced support this week.

The Conservative case, as Lorne Doerkson’s party states it, is a commitment to work with the federal government to fund and build the Expo Line extension to Newton Town Centre. Surrey mayor-elect Doug McCallum has favoured that wording. He says the Conservatives made an explicit commitment to build the line, and he endorsed Doerkson’s party at a Surrey rally on Thursday.

The NDP case, as David Eby’s party states it, is that it also supports building the extension, matching a promise McCallum made in the civic campaign. The week before, the NDP promised $250 million toward TransLink’s proposed $700-million King George Boulevard bus rapid transit line from Surrey City Centre to Semiahmoo Town Centre. Its later announcement says that money could be redirected to help advance a Newton SkyTrain extension instead. McCallum says the NDP has only expressed a willingness to discuss the project.

Polls are open today, Saturday, October 24, from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. Daily Hive reports the next government will still have to set budgets, construction timelines and, in some cases, federal agreements before either version of the line is delivered. # Vancouver Daily News
> **891,348 British Columbians have already voted ahead of Saturday's election.**

**What You Need to Know:** 891,348 British Columbians have already voted ahead of Saturday's election, a smaller advance turnout than in 2024, and election-day ballots will be counted by hand. A B.C. court has convicted Adam Mann of second-degree murder in the 2024 killing of Tori Dunn in her Surrey home. Langley RCMP are investigating an alleged assault on a driving instructor in a church parking lot; the woman arrested has not been charged.

### Top Stories
**What advance voting numbers tell us about the B.C. election: Vancouver Sun**
Elections B.C. recorded 891,348 advance votes from October 16 to 21, about 24 per cent of registered voters, compared with 1,001,331 and about 28 per cent in 2024. CBC reports that advance voting is down 11 per cent from 2024. David Black, a political-science professor at Royal Roads University, told the Sun that advance turnout is not a reliable indicator of election-day turnout, and that a large undecided block plus a snap election called during a municipal campaign may have held numbers down. CityNews reports that Elections B.C. says ballots cast on election day Saturday will be counted by hand. Black said advance ballots, already tabulated electronically, are likely to be released sooner than Saturday's hand count. Advance turnout rose in Surrey-Serpentine River and in Vancouver-Quilchena, where OneBC leader Dallas Brodie is running, and fell across most of Surrey and Vancouver, including 22 per cent versus 24 per cent in Surrey and 22 per cent versus 27 per cent in Vancouver. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/what-advance-voting-numbers-tell-us-about-bc-election) Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/advance-voting-bc-provincial-election-9.7392658?cmp=rss) Source: [vancouver.citynews.ca](https://vancouver.citynews.ca/2026/10/23/bc-election-ballots-to-be-counted-by-hand/)

**Guilty verdict issued in 2024 Surrey home-invasion murder of Tori Dunn: CBC**
A court has convicted Adam Mann of second-degree murder in the killing of Surrey resident Tori Dunn during a home invasion two years ago. Global News reports that Dunn, 30, was stabbed four times, including an 18-centimetre wound to her abdomen that killed her, and two defensive wounds to her hands. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/adam-mann-second-degree-murder-verdict-tori-dunn-9.7392012?cmp=rss) Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12113826/adam-mann-guilty-second-degree-murder-death-tori-dunn-surrey-home/)

**Video captures woman allegedly assaulting driving instructor in Langley: Global BC**
Langley RCMP say they are investigating an assault in a church parking lot in the 4800 block of 207 Street at about 9 a.m. Wednesday, and that a driving instructor was assaulted. Cpl. Mansoor Sahak said officers arrested a woman at the scene; she has been released, has not been charged, and is expected to appear in court. Video circulating online appears to show a woman assaulting the instructor while saying, "Go back to your country." The driving school said it strongly condemns the racism and aggressive behaviour depicted in the video. RCMP are asking anyone who witnessed the incident to speak with investigators. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12114129/video-of-assault-on-langley-driving-instructor/)

### City & Province
**Daniel Fontaine hopes to move on Metro Vancouver accountability charter: Vancouver Sun**
New Westminster mayor-elect Daniel Fontaine says he will push a five-point Metro Vancouver accountability charter after October 17, when 14 of 21 municipalities elected new mayors. West Vancouver mayor-elect Kirk LaPointe and White Rock mayor-elect Chris Shields have also signed. The charter calls for no extra pay for mayors on Metro's board and committees, a transparent review of cost overruns at the North Shore wastewater treatment plant, a smaller mayors' council, an auditor general for Metro and its municipalities, and an independent critical services review. Fontaine said Metro has 41 directors and has spread into housing, parks and an investment arm; he wants a review, not abolition, and will bring the charter to Metro if New Westminster council votes him onto the board. LaPointe said Metro should be smaller in mandate or directly elected, with oversight and more transparency. Coquitlam mayor-elect Craig Hodge has not signed but said he supports the reforms, that some are already being looked at, and that the public has lost confidence. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/daniel-fontaine-hopes-to-move-on-metro-vancouver-accountability-charter)

**Vancouver Island's Duncan Showroom closing doors end of November: CBC British Columbia**
The Duncan Showroom, open in some form for more than 23 years, is set to close at the end of November because the lease is not being renewed, its artistic director says, unless a new location is found. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/duncan-showroom-closing-doors-end-november-9.7392535?cmp=rss)

### The Closer Look
**Health care a major election issue as B.C. doctor says he's hit breaking point: Global BC**
Dr. Kevin McLeod, an internal medicine specialist at Lions Gate Hospital, says he has hit a breaking point and is seriously considering resigning from the hospital. He posted Thursday that doing a specialist consult on a complex patient in 20 minutes is not safe: if he takes longer, urgent care is delayed and the pile gets bigger. He told Global News this week has been especially difficult and is taking a toll on him and his family. On a typical call day, he said, he might have 20 to 22 new complex patients and another 35 to 50 people in an office. What tipped it, he said, was Sechelt phoning to send patients to Lions Gate because Sechelt hospital has no physician capacity.

Patients who need neurological care at Penticton Regional Hospital could see reduced access to specialist services after three neurologists resigned their hospital privileges. The resignations followed a change Interior Health introduced last month requiring neurologists to provide on-call services across the entire health region. Dr. Adam Thompson, president of Doctors of B.C., said there are always concerns when a facility loses doctors. He said the new on-call rule would substantially increase workload without additional support in their communities, that neurologists are already in short supply, and that there is a tipping point where those cases cannot all be juggled at once.

McLeod wants the next government to make people in highly paid administrative jobs accountable. He said the number of people in those admin roles has risen sharply, and he would not argue the system is being run more efficiently. With the provincial election days away, B.C. NDP leader David Eby promised to put minimum nurse-to-patient ratios into law so health authorities and hospital managers know where a government he leads would go. B.C. Nurses' Union president Adriane Gear said ratio legislation is a chance to build on progress already made, give patients and nurses more certainty, and support a planned expansion of ratios in emergency departments, operating rooms, long-term care, assisted living, and community and non-hospital care. She said safe staffing has to outlast party politics and stay a commitment no matter which party forms government. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12114363/health-care-major-election-issue-bc-doctor-breaking-point/)

### Also Today
**B.C. communities earn C+ grades for quality of life, with housing getting lowest marks: CityNews Vancouver**
Residents across Metro Vancouver, Vancouver Island and the Okanagan give their communities an average grade of C+ for quality of life, with housing the lowest marks. Source: [vancouver.citynews.ca](https://vancouver.citynews.ca/2026/10/23/bc-quality-of-life-poll/)

### Getting Around

Exit 23 from Highway 99 to Ladner Trunk Road in Delta is closed through today, and paving on Highway 1A in Surrey closes the bridge and the northbound lanes from 9 p.m. tonight until 5 a.m. Monday, with southbound lanes staying open. Eastbound Highway 1 lanes stay closed around 256th Street through October 31, with traffic shifted north of the median and crossing back near Lefeuvre Road. No weather warnings are in effect: Friday clears after morning fog, with a high of 12 and a low of 7, and Saturday is cloudy with a 60 per cent chance of showers, a high of 11, and rain overnight. Source: [drivebc.ca](https://www.drivebc.ca/) Source: [weather.gc.ca](https://weather.gc.ca/rss/weather/49.245_-123.115_e.xml)

### Sports
**Raymond scores twice, Red Wings hand Canucks ninth straight loss: NHL.com**
The Canucks lost 5-2 to the Detroit Red Wings, a ninth straight loss that dropped them to last in the NHL after the Los Angeles Kings and Calgary Flames each moved a point ahead. Lucas Raymond scored twice, Elias Pettersson scored on the power play, and Jonathan Lekkerimäki also scored; Vancouver was outshot 31-13 and had no shot on goal in the entire second period. Brock Boeser called the disconnect embarrassing, and head coach Manny Malhotra said the effort level was a little disappointing and that many of the mistakes were effort-based. Source: [nhl.com](https://www.nhl.com/news/detroit-red-wings-vancouver-canucks-game-recap-october-22-2026) Source: [dailyhive.com](https://dailyhive.com/vancouver/i-watched-this-game-boeser-canucks-last-place-ninth-straight-loss)

**Larraz Scores As 10-man Whitecaps Hold Off LAFC In Tight Tie: Yahoo Sports**
Larraz scored as the Whitecaps, reduced to 10 men, held LAFC to a tie. Source: [sports.yahoo.com](https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/larraz-scores-10-man-whitecaps-130000580.html)

**Bombers have one last chance at playoff bid but Lions stand in the way: CBC British Columbia**
The B.C. Lions, at 10-7, have already clinched a playoff spot and host the Winnipeg Blue Bombers, at 8-9, in Vancouver on Friday, then host the West Division semifinal on October 31 regardless of Friday's result. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/manitoba/winnipeg-blue-bombers-bc-lions-cfl-9.7392035?cmp=rss)

### Both Sides: Grocery prices
The B.C. NDP and the B.C. Greens are offering plans to lower grocery costs in the provincial campaign. The B.C. Conservatives say tax cuts, not shelf-price rules, are the way to help people pay for food. Voters finish casting ballots on Saturday.

NDP leader David Eby wants a cap on the mark-up on essentials such as milk, eggs, cheese, butter and poultry, applied to corporate retailers. He singled out Loblaws, Save-On-Foods, Walmart, Costco and Sobeys, which operates Safeway. The Greens propose government-owned and government-managed grocery stores, starting with 20 stores and a $100 million investment, sourcing local products and selling a basket of core goods 30 per cent below market prices. The Conservatives say lowering taxes puts more money in people's pockets for groceries.

Chris Bodnar, an assistant professor of agriculture at the University of the Fraser Valley, says milk is often a loss leader, with thin or negative margins, used to pull shoppers toward other goods. He says a cap gets attention but does not solve the problem, and that it misses climate change, conflicts that raise fertilizer and fuel costs, and the land and water B.C. needs to grow more food. The Vancouver Sun cites a Harvard Business School study that found small, temporary relief on capped items while major grocers raised prices on other products, and says the International Monetary Fund advises against broad grocery price controls because they send the wrong signals and can disrupt supply, preferring cash transfers. Hungary has capped staples since 2022 and, in 2025, capped retail profit at 10 per cent on more than 30 essential foods. France in 2023 negotiated a price freeze with major chains instead of legislating one.

Tammara Soma, an associate professor at Simon Fraser University, says public stores would give shoppers and farmers another option. She points to about 240 U.S. military commissaries, where shoppers save an average of 25 per cent, and to Mexico's subsidized stores selling staples below market prices. She says the five main B.C. grocers sometimes will not buy produce that looks slightly off, and a public outlet could take that food. The Sun notes that government-run stores carry an ongoing cost. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/bc-election-analysis-ndp-greens-promise-to-reduce-grocery-costs)

# Vancouver Daily News
> **Seventy percent of Vancouver voters want a site for one hundred involuntary-care beds.**

**What You Need to Know:** Vancouver plebiscite results released Wednesday show 70 percent of voters want a site for 100 involuntary-care beds, and voters said yes to both drug-use questions championed by outgoing mayor Ken Sim. A rabid skunk in the downtown West End has already led Vancouver Coastal Health to vaccinate a small number of people who were bitten. James Bryant is expected to enter a plea today in Seattle on a foreign-murder conspiracy charge tied to Tumbler Ridge.

### Top Stories
**Vancouver residents vote yes on 2 plebiscite questions regarding drug use: CBC British Columbia**
Voters said yes to both plebiscite questions championed by outgoing mayor Ken Sim. One question proposed strengthening city laws to forbid open-air hard drug use. The other proposed pushing the province for more involuntary care at a soon-to-be-closed downtown hospital site. The Vancouver Sun reports that results released Wednesday show 70 percent of voters want a site for 100 involuntary-care beds, and that voters were overwhelmingly opposed to open-air drug use. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/vancouver-plebiscite-2026-drug-use-results-9.7390927?cmp=rss) Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/vancouver-plebiscite-voters-overwhelmingly-opposed-to-open-air-drug-use)

**Alleged Tumbler Ridge mass shooting conspirator set to enter plea in U.S. court: Global BC**
James Bryant, 30, is expected to enter a plea Thursday at an arraignment in a Seattle courthouse, after a Washington state grand jury indicted Bryant for conspiracy to murder persons in a foreign country. Bryant, who uses female pronouns and goes by Melody, has been denied bail. A U.S. Justice Department statement says that charge is punishable by up to life in prison and cautions that the accusations remain unproven. The complaint alleges Bryant colluded online with Jesse Van Rootselaar, who killed eight people in Tumbler Ridge last February, including five students and an educational assistant, before fatally shooting herself. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12113039/james-bryant-tumbler-ridge-plea/)

**Grand Forks, B.C., doctor charged with two counts of sexual assault: CBC British Columbia**
Dr. Nathan Gordon Dalla Lana, a physician practicing in B.C.'s West Kootenay, has been charged with two counts of sexual assault involving two people on August 10, 2026. The charges are accusations. Nothing in the report is a finding of guilt. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/grand-forks-doctor-charged-sexual-assault-9.7390847?cmp=rss)

### City & Province
**Dease Lake, B.C., suspends fire department services as volunteer numbers dwindle: CBC British Columbia**
Fire protection services in Dease Lake have been suspended until further notice after the volunteer fire department dwindled to two trained members. The regional district is recruiting firefighters to restore service. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/dease-lake-fire-department-closure-9.7391079?cmp=rss)

### The Closer Look
**'Small number of people' bitten by rabid skunk in downtown Vancouver: Daily Hive Vancouver**
Vancouver Coastal Health says a skunk from downtown Vancouver has tested positive for rabies, and a small number of people bitten by that skunk have already been assessed and given rabies vaccinations and immunoglobulin. The Vancouver Sun reports that a man was bitten in the West End. Castanet reports the health authority confirmed the case in a Wednesday news release and described rabies as a viral infection that affects the brain and nervous system.

Vancouver Coastal Health says the virus sits in the saliva of an infected animal and can pass through a bite or, less commonly, a scratch. The authority says it is not transmitted through a skunk's spray, urine, or feces. People are being asked to come forward if, between September 22 and October 17, they were bitten or scratched, or if they handled, picked up, or otherwise had direct contact with a sick or abnormally behaving skunk in downtown Vancouver's West End and Stanley Park area. Castanet says anyone who lives outside the Vancouver Coastal Health region and may have had that contact should call their own local health authority.

For people inside the region, Vancouver Coastal Health says to call public health immediately at 604-675-3900, open Monday to Friday from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., so a health professional can assess the contact. After those hours, the authority says to go to an urgent care centre or an emergency department. If someone believes they were bitten, Vancouver Coastal Health says to wash the wound with soap and warm water for at least 15 minutes and seek immediate medical care. Pet owners who think an animal met the skunk are told to call a veterinarian promptly and say the pet may have been exposed to a rabid skunk.

The same notice asks anyone who sees a wild animal, including a skunk, acting abnormally to call the B.C. Report All Poachers and Polluters line at 1-877-952-7277. Abnormal, in the authority's wording, can mean disoriented, sick, injured, stumbling, active at unusual times of day, showing no fear of people, or aggressive. The practical change is for anyone who had direct contact in that window, and for anyone walking a pet through the West End or Stanley Park: the assessment line is open on weekdays, and after hours the instruction is urgent care or an emergency department, not a wait until morning. **Stalled Downtown Vancouver office tower project pivots to 295-room hotel: Daily Hive Vancouver**
A narrow vacant lot at 619 West Hastings Street, approved years ago for offices, is now the subject of a hotel-heavy revision. Vancouver city council approved Uptown Property Group's rezoning in May 2020 for a 28-storey tower, 330 feet or 100.5 metres, with about 158,000 square feet of office space. A development permit for that all-office plan was issued in September 2022. It never advanced into construction. Daily Hive reports the stall followed weak office demand coming out of the pandemic.

The revised development permit was submitted this past summer and made public yesterday, ahead of formal public consultation. It calls for 32 storeys and 362 feet, or 110.5 metres, with almost 158,000 square feet of floor area. Levels two to 24 would switch from offices to a boutique hotel. Two hundred ninety-five guest rooms would occupy levels three through 24, about 126,000 square feet of hotel space. Levels 25 to 31 would remain offices, about 32,000 square feet, with a shared outdoor amenity deck on the roof. The mid-block site sits immediately east of the historic Royal Bank Building, near Granville Street and West Hastings Street. The hotel pitch leans on proximity to the Vancouver Convention Centre, frequent buses, and Waterfront Station for the Expo Line, the Canada Line and the SeaBus.

The revision keeps a distinctive piece of the earlier design: physically connecting the new tower to the 1931 bank so the new concrete walls and core can brace that building in an earthquake. Musson Cattell Mackey Partnership designed both concepts. It says work affecting the heritage building, including those structural connections and an enclosure over the existing light well, would be covered by a separate permit. Sumner Godfrey Davenport, Royal Bank's chief architect from 1920 to 1942, designed the bank with the company's then Montreal headquarters in mind. **99 B-Line, the busiest bus route in Metro Vancouver, could be renamed in 2027: Daily Hive**
Daily Hive reports that TransLink is discussing a new name for the bus that would replace the 99 B-Line when the Millennium Line's Broadway extension opens in late 2027. The busiest bus route in Metro Vancouver would then run only between the University of British Columbia and the new Arbutus Station. Its segment between Arbutus Street and Commercial-Broadway Station would be discontinued. That would be the route's second major shortening in a 30-year history. BC Transit launched the 99 B-Line in 1996 between UBC and Lougheed Mall, beyond Commercial-Broadway along Lougheed Highway in Burnaby. After the Millennium Line opened in 2002, TransLink shortened it to what is now Commercial-Broadway Station and kept the name. A TransLink spokesperson told Daily Hive that discussions are under way about a potential name change, that no final decision has been made, and that further details will be announced in the coming months. The B-Line brand meant faster, frequent, limited-stop service using 60-foot, three-door buses. The 98 B-Line ran from downtown Vancouver to Richmond on Granville Street from 2000 until the Canada Line opened in 2009. The 97 B-Line, from 2002, linked Lougheed Town Centre Station and Coquitlam Centre until the Evergreen extension in 2016. The 96 B-Line launched in 2013 on 104 Avenue and King George Boulevard between Guildford Town Centre and Newton, and the 95 B-Line ran Hastings Street between downtown and Simon Fraser University's Burnaby Mountain campus. In 2020 TransLink retired the B-Line name on every remaining route except the 99 and introduced RapidBus. The 96 became the R1 King George Boulevard RapidBus and the 95 the R5 Hastings Street RapidBus, joined that year by the R2 Marine Drive, R3 Lougheed Highway and R4 41st Avenue routes. The R6 Scott Road RapidBus followed in 2024. RapidBus added bus-priority lanes on some sections, stop signs with route information, real-time arrival displays and bright green branding. Dozens of articulated buses serve the 99, especially at peak. TransLink has projected the shortened route could reach capacity as soon as the extension opens to Arbutus, because the subway is expected to draw new riders and existing riders from other buses even with a transfer at Arbutus for the remaining trip to UBC. Arbutus Station could become one of the SkyTrain network's busiest stations when the extension opens. TransLink says the 99 now has peak capacity of about 1,800 passengers per hour per direction. With the Broadway extension, Millennium Line capacity is expected to rise to 7,100 passengers per hour per direction, with trains every three minutes at peak. In 2025 the 99 had nearly 10.7 million boardings, averaging 34,700 on a weekday, 20,700 on a Saturday and 15,100 on a Sunday or holiday. When the line is extended from Arbutus to UBC, potentially in the 2030s, the express bus would be fully discontinued. TransLink is also proposing Bus Rapid Transit, with more bus-priority measures and passenger amenities than RapidBus or the B-Line. **Two soldiers from B.C. among four dead in CFB Wainwright fire: Vancouver Sun**
The Vancouver Sun reports that two of the four Canadian Armed Forces members killed in a fire at CFB Wainwright were from B.C. Major-General L.W. Rutland, Commander of 1st Canadian Division, said Sunday afternoon that three of the men were with the Third Battalion, Princess Patricia’s Canadian Light Infantry, based at CFB Edmonton, and that the fourth was from the Loyal Edmonton Regiment. The PPCLI soldiers killed are Pte. Aidan Goulding, Pte. Shaun Farrell and Pte. Hayden Lykkemark. The Loyal Edmonton member is Sgt. Morgan Wong, from Edmonton. Rutland said the four were killed during an outdoor exercise on a section attack range when a fire swept into the area. He said he spoke to his commander on the ground Saturday night and Sunday morning, and that commander said that within 30 seconds to a minute they saw no fire, and then there was a fire right on top of them. Premier Danielle Smith said Sunday afternoon that 39 soldiers were injured, including 19 critically. Acute Care Alberta said in a Sunday afternoon statement that 30 units, including ground ambulances, planes and helicopters, took patients to hospitals in Edmonton, Red Deer and Calgary. Farrell’s mother, Patricia, posted on Facebook that her son Shaun had died, thanking people for love, support and prayers. In a separate post Saturday night she had said Shaun was at CFB Wainwright taking part in the training and asked people to pray for him. A post earlier this year, the Sun reports, said Shaun had only recently joined the military. Kim Goulding posted that Aidan was bright, kind and proud to serve, that he had just graduated in August, and that he was way too young. The Loyal Edmonton Regiment is a reserve regiment. Wong, a University of Alberta graduate, had been with the Forces since 2017, according to his LinkedIn page, and in his day job over the past three years had worked in the Treasury Board Secretariat and in Hospital and Surgical Health Services. ### The Closer Look
**The Bookless Club: What are your 'deer in the headlights' encounters?: Vancouver Sun**
Jane Macdougall, writing in the Vancouver Sun, describes four Columbian black-tailed deer grazing on the wrong side of the road at Qualicum Beach. She identifies them as the native, compact subspecies of mule deer that inhabit Vancouver Island. They had been drawn, she writes, to a verdant strip of grass in a section of waterfront park. At some point they would have to cross a two-lane roadway back to a wooded slope. A Peterbilt truck rumbled past in the opposite direction. Swerving, let alone stopping, was not an option for that truck, she writes.
The column then sets that scene against provincial collision counts. Each year in B.C. there are about 12,500 wildlife collisions. More than 9,400 deer-and-vehicle collisions account for 80 per cent of those accidents. Such crashes result in close to 900 human injuries each year and an average of four fatalities. The cost to the provincial government for animal-related claims is more than $41 million, and Macdougall stresses that figure is annual.
She also recounts a family crash with a different animal. An uncle, driving home one night, broadsided a moose and spent weeks in hospital. His car was a write-off. A moose can weigh 1,500 pounds, or 680 kilograms, she writes, and when a driver hits one, the heavy body tends to launch onto the hood and through the windshield. She says two lives are oftentimes lost in that kind of collision. Not every wildlife crash is a direct hit on the animal. Sometimes the driver smashes into something other than the creature, and the outcome can be just as bad for the car and its occupants.
Macdougall writes that she used to wish rental cars in rural areas came with a deer whistle, an inexpensive, wind-activated ultrasonic whistle that attaches under a car and is meant to warn wildlife. There is no statistical evidence that these devices work, she writes. Wildlife may not react as hoped. How far the sound carries, whether that is enough time to brake, and whether wind or a nearby river drowns it out are open questions in the column. The only thing authorities advise, she writes, is to drive slower and with extreme caution at dusk and dawn, to always expect deer to be in clusters, and to brake rather than swerve if wildlife is on the road ahead. She lives in Vancouver and writes The Bookless Club on Saturdays in the Sun. > **Forty-nine percent of the vote made Melissa Granum Delta's new mayor Saturday night.**

**What You Need to Know:** Melissa Granum is Delta's new mayor after taking 49 percent of the vote Saturday night, ahead of Dylan Kruger and George Harvie. Across Metro Vancouver, unofficial counts also put new mayors in Richmond and Surrey and returned Mike Hurley in Burnaby. Highway 99 paving in Vancouver runs through Monday morning, with a mild, mainly sunny Sunday and no weather alerts.

### Top Stories
**Melissa Granum elected mayor of Delta:** Vancouver Sun
Melissa Granum won the Delta mayoral race with 49 percent of the vote, 14,988 ballots, in results the Vancouver Sun reported at 10 p.m. Dylan Kruger was second with 28 percent, 8,567 votes, and George Harvie third with 23 percent, 6,985. The Sun said the early figures were advance and mail-in votes, and that Granum's lead held as more polls reported. Granum told the Sun there had been "a groundswell of support for hope for the future, and transparent governance and change," and that the campaign had been "about everyday residents working together for change." Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/bc-municipal-election-day-2026-updates-results-reaction)

**Doug McCallum unseats Brenda Locke in Surrey:** Vancouver Sun
Former mayor Doug McCallum unseated incumbent Brenda Locke, taking 31.9 percent of the vote to Locke's 23 percent with all 164 polls reporting, 42,741 votes to 30,886. Locke conceded just before 10 p.m., telling a solemn crowd, "Surrey voters have definitely spoken and this was not the result we counted on," then congratulated McCallum and, asked if she would run again, said, "Never say never." McCallum said, "We will address affordability, we will address your safety, and we will address your infrastructure," and said he planned to appoint Mandeep Nagra as deputy mayor. Mike Starchuk finished with 12.9 percent and Linda Annis with 12.39 percent. Safe Surrey won a council majority; the only councillor not on that slate is incumbent Harry Bains, from Locke's team, who received the most votes of any candidate. The rest of council is incumbents Doug Elford and Mandeep Nagra, former councillors Allison Patton and Laurie Guerra, and newcomers Meera Gill, Suhana Gill and Cheney Cloke. Elford called the result surprising and said residents could expect the slate to carry out its promises, including a four-year property-tax freeze, purchasing a police helicopter and seeking funding for another Surrey hospital, "as best as we can." A Leger poll for Postmedia News, conducted Sept. 23 to 30, had suggested Locke would receive a second term. Advance voting was 52,600 ballots, about 15 percent of registered voters, up 47 percent from 35,701 advance votes in 2022. McCallum previously served as mayor from 1996 to 2005 and from 2018 until his loss to Locke in 2022; Locke won that race by less than 1,000 votes. The Sun reported the two became rivals over policing, with McCallum wanting a municipal force and Locke wanting to keep the RCMP. ### The Closer Look
**Mike Hurley wins third term as Burnaby mayor:** Freshet News
Mike Hurley has won a third term as mayor of Burnaby, and the Burnaby Citizens Association kept a majority on city council. Freshet News reported unofficial results from Saturday's vote. Hurley won a six-way mayoral race with 28,946 votes, 58.43 percent of 50,326 ballots cast. Burnaby First candidate Heymann Yip was second with 9,250 votes, 18.67 percent.

He thanked residents for electing him to another four years and said, "It's an amazing journey, an opportunity to get out there and help people, which is something that I live to do."

The council ballot had 42 candidates and several new parties. The BCA majority held. Three BCA incumbents did not run: Sav Dhaliwal, Pietro Calendino and Alison Gu. Three new BCA candidates were elected in their place: Cindy Lee, Ryan Erwin and Kiran Singh. New Burnaby Party incumbent Richard Lee remains the only non-BCA member of council. Freshet News said it was unable to reach Lee for comment on election night.

Joe Keithley, first elected with the Burnaby Green Party and switched to the BCA in December, led the council count with 18,073 votes, 5.51 percent. Cindy Lee was next with 17,429, 5.32 percent, then Ryan Erwin with 16,476, 5.03 percent. Lee said she had not expected that finish and credited support from her own community and from running with the BCA team. She said many residents had read the candidates' profiles and recognized her while she was door-knocking, and that "in Burnaby, our residents are really responsible. That's why we have a great city."

Incumbent BCA councillors Maita Santiago and Daniel Tetrault each kept a seat for a second term, with 16,292 votes, 4.97 percent, and 15,288, 4.66 percent. Richard Lee also won a second term, with 13,257 votes, 4.04 percent. Kiran Singh took the last council seat, finishing 1,180 votes ahead of independent Allen Chen: Singh had 13,209 votes, 4.03 percent, and Chen 12,029, 3.67 percent.

Voter turnout in Burnaby rose to 29.23 percent of eligible voters, from 19.7 percent in 2022. Source: [freshetnews.ca](https://www.freshetnews.ca/mike-hurley-wins-third-term-as-burnaby-mayor/)

Mohammed Arif Ansari, twenty-seven, is charged with two counts of second-degree murder and one count of indignity to human remains in the twenty twenty-two killings of Coquitlam couple Kiesha Garie, thirty-one, and her fiancée, Umair Kasim, thirty. ### The Closer Look
**Chinese state-owned XCMG facing lawsuits alleging it defrauded Canadian equipment dealers: Global BC**
At Vancouver's law courts on Friday, veteran heavy-equipment dealer Ryan Martin said a business that was good for years has wrecked his family. His company, Arctic Machinery, with dealerships in Prince George, Chilliwack and Kelowna, started selling machines from Chinese state-owned manufacturer XCMG in twenty seventeen. Martin said business was good until about twenty twenty-one. "It's destroyed our family," he told Global News. XCMG is one of the world's largest manufacturers of heavy equipment. Martin said the quality changed several years ago: "The quality of the equipment that time was not what the quality was in the past."

Civil lawsuits now allege that XCMG defrauded equipment dealers in Canada. Martin said other Canadian XCMG dealers hit similar problems and, in troubleshooting them, found what they describe as evidence of a process "of changing serial number plates and changing the years of the machines in order to maybe misrepresent to the end user what they were buying." His example was a machine built in twenty twenty and sold to the dealer as a twenty twenty-two. In July, a Saskatchewan dealer sued XCMG, alleging unlawful tampering with serial-number plates on equipment sold in Alberta this year. LTR Equipment, based in Quebec, filed a similar case. A lift company in Ontario has also filed, alleging serial numbers were tampered with.

XCMG Canada told Global News: "Arctic Machinery purchased approximately $18 million in XCMG-branded inventory, which it did not pay for." The company said it "is fully defending the claims in the civil actions." Martin said the family firm was forced into bankruptcy when XCMG called in its loans, which he said was retaliation for blowing the whistle on the alleged tampering. The people and companies in these suits are accusing and defending, not convicted of a crime. RCMP in Alberta's K Division confirmed that members of their auto theft unit carried out a search warrant at XCMG's headquarters in April and that the investigation is ongoing. For Arctic Machinery, the fight is already a bankruptcy. For buyers of those machines, the allegation is that a serial plate and a model year may not have matched the equipment they thought they were getting. ### Both Sides: Compensation when Crown land moves to First Nations
A leaked provincial briefing and a presentation dated September tenth outline a commitment to transfer four hundred parcels of Crown land to First Nations, and proposals to limit, through Forest Act changes, what timber-rights holders would be paid, citing continuing fiscal constraints. The presentation landed less than two weeks before Premier David Eby called a snap election. Kim Haakstad, chief executive of the Council of Forest Industries, said she first learned of the proposal in early August under non-disclosure agreements, and is speaking now because reporter Rob Shaw made the documents public on Northern Beat.

Speaking as NDP leader, Eby said the list comes from "very public, discussed agreements with treaty First Nations," some signed more than a decade ago under previous governments, and that the documents are proposals to reduce the cost of those transfers. His best reason is the taxpayer: "to drive down the cost of that, so that taxpayers aren’t bearing the cost of that, is absolutely crucial." He said even B.C. Conservative leader Lorne Doerkson agrees that agreements with First Nations are part of the path forward, and that some transfers clear the way for forestry where "court challenges to forest tenures, to cutting permits and other things" have left the industry stalled.

Haakstad said timber companies support reconciliation and understand that those agreements need to happen. Her objection is who pays. "We think this proposal should not go forward," she said. "We think it is not acceptable to have us pay for these costs, especially at this time when the sector is in a deepening crisis." B.C. Conservative candidate Scott McInnis called the behind-closed-doors proposal unethical and "absolutely abhorrent," a betrayal of an industry "begging this government for some action and some support." He said the party supports partnerships that advance quality of life for Indigenous people, and that the public is not willing to accept agreements made behind closed doors. Vancouver lawyer Wes Mussio said that where a transfer is meant to let forestry proceed, government would open itself to "quite a few legal disputes." Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/local-news/b-c-forest-industry-bristles-at-proposal-to-reduce-compensation-in-first-nation-land-transfers)
