# Vancouver Daily News
> **Eby promised Thursday to scrap the forty-five-dollar bus pass for low-income seniors.**

**What You Need to Know:** NDP Leader David Eby promised Thursday in Surrey to scrap the forty-five-dollar bus pass fee for low-income seniors and to let more people qualify. The same stop put two hundred and fifty million dollars toward bus rapid transit between Surrey and White Rock, while other parties offered their own promises and a leaked Crown-land note drew questions. Homicide investigators are still trying to name a man found dead in Surrey, and Vancouver police are looking into reports of AI images of female students at Sir Winston Churchill Secondary.

### Top Stories
**Eby promises a free senior bus pass on a Surrey campaign stop: Global News**
A day after the leaders' debate, NDP Leader David Eby was back in Surrey on Thursday and promised, if re-elected, to drop the forty-five-dollar bus pass fee for low-income seniors, to let more people qualify, and to put two hundred and fifty million dollars toward bus rapid transit between Surrey and White Rock, working with the federal government. The Vancouver Sun also reports that he said a re-elected NDP would keep building the Surrey-to-Langley SkyTrain. Most questions he faced concerned a leaked briefing note, first obtained by Northern Beat, which the Sun says shows the province developing legislation to transfer four hundred plots of Crown land to First Nations without compensating forestry companies. Eby said many of those plots sit in agreements going back years, including under Christy Clark's B.C. Liberal government, and that the proposal is meant to cut the fiscal cost of those obligations in a sector that has faced mill closures and job losses. Conservative Leader Lorne Doerkson had no public events Thursday; his party promised a new women and children's hospital in Surrey. Green Leader Emily Lowan said she would lift the minimum wage by more than inflation every year until it hits a living wage, widen sectoral bargaining, and reverse direct-to-consumer alcohol delivery, which she said would open the B.C. Liquor Distribution Branch to privatization. CentreBC Leader Elenore Sturko said she would add five hundred RCMP officers to the provincial business line, one hundred a year over five years, and said that line has stayed at two thousand six hundred and two; the Conservatives also said Jordan McIntosh will no longer be their Vancouver-Strathcona candidate after he was accused of posting remarks about Hitler and the Holocaust, and that if elected he will not sit in caucus. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12104245/bc-party-leaders-campaign-transit-massey-tunnel-safety/) Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/bc-election-sparks-fly-over-contentious-issues-following-leaders-tv-debate-no-winner)

**IHIT seeks the name of a man found dead in Surrey: Vancouver Sun**
Around 1 p.m. Wednesday, Surrey police and firefighters went to the sixty-one-hundred block of 156th Street after calls about a body at the roadside. An adult man was pronounced dead at the scene. Foul play is suspected, and the Integrated Homicide Investigation Team has taken the file. Sergeant Freda Fong of IHIT said the case is in its early stages, a forensic examination of the scene is underway, and investigators need a timeline of events before the death. Anyone who was in that block between October 8 and October 14, or who has dashcam or other information, is asked to contact IHIT. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/police-ask-for-help-to-identify-body-found-on-surrey-roadside)

**Vancouver police investigate reported AI images at Churchill Secondary: Global News**
Vancouver police and the Vancouver School Board are investigating reports of inappropriate online behaviour involving some Grade 12 students at Sir Winston Churchill Secondary. Global News reports talk among students last week that some male Grade 12 students had made AI content of female students; what that content shows is not established, and parents believe it is sexual. A parent identified only as Gene, who has a daughter in Grade 12, said some of the allegations are pretty disgusting and vile, and said a principal's email told families the school was working with police. The school board said it is taking the matter seriously, gathering information, supporting students who may have been affected, and will not share details about individual students. Police said they are in contact with the school and the board and that an investigation is underway. Criminal defence lawyer Michael Shapray told Global News the Criminal Code on child exploitation material was amended in the summer of 2026 so that artificially generated images with a person's likeness fall within that definition. Global News has learned at least one student received a short suspension; how many students are involved is not known. ### The Closer Look
**'Heavy distractions' stalling the Greater Vancouver housing market: Vancouver Sun**
A Royal LePage market survey released Thursday shows sales and prices down across Greater Vancouver, with further price drops expected in the final quarter of 2026. The aggregate price of a home fell four per cent year over year to one point one million dollars in the third quarter. The median price of a single-family detached home fell five point six per cent to two million dollars. The median condo price fell four point one per cent to seven hundred and ten thousand dollars. Transaction volumes are running twenty-five to thirty per cent below the ten-year average.

Randy Ryalls, managing broker at Royal LePage Sterling Realty, oversees one hundred and twenty realtors from Vancouver to Maple Ridge. He told the Vancouver Sun that 2021 felt like fifty buyers for every home listed, and that he now sees fifty listings for every buyer. More choice and less competition have not been enough to move many people off the sidelines. Ryalls called geopolitical tensions, a trade war, and the coming elections "heavy distractions" that have people putting major moves on hold. He said the development industry has virtually ground to a halt, buyers are no longer lining up for pre-construction sales, and the investor class has gone quiet, with some shifting capital to Alberta and Washington State. A mom-and-pop investor who might have bought one apartment building in Vancouver might afford two or three in Calgary, he said. He listed rent controls, restrictions, and the property transfer tax among the reasons B.C. looks less attractive, and said that does not help when the market is already slow.

Ryalls said many of Vancouver's unsold units are small and were built with short-term rentals or international students in mind. Those markets dried up when government policy changed. There is also uncertainty over mortgage rates. Inflation may cause the Bank of Canada to raise rates, and owners who locked in during 2021 and 2022 are looking at significantly higher rates when they renew. Royal LePage president and chief executive Phil Soper said he expects the bank to hold rates through 2026, with an increase more likely in early 2027. He said the prospect of higher borrowing costs usually draws some buyers in sooner, but low confidence is outweighing the urgency to lock in today's rates. The report notes Canada's busy political calendar. In B.C., municipal elections will be followed a week later by a provincial election. Soper said elections can give buyers and sellers a reason to pause while they judge what a change in government might mean, and that a home is a long-term commitment to a community. Ryalls said stalled development can leave too little supply later: if a developer cannot sell for the cost to build, housing does not get built. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/heavy-distractions-stalling-greater-vancouver-bc-housing-market-report)

Vancouver was clear and 7.7 degrees; Friday is mainly sunny as morning fog patches dissipate, with a high of 17 except 21 inland and a moderate UV index of 3, then a few showers Friday night and a low of 11, a 60 per cent chance of morning showers Saturday clearing later with a high of 16 and morning gusts to 50 near the water, and a sunny Sunday with a high of 12. ### Sports
**Tkachuk's hat trick lifts the Panthers over the Canucks 3-2 in overtime: Langley Advance Times**
Brady Tkachuk scored three times as the Florida Panthers rallied for a 3-2 overtime win over the Vancouver Canucks on Thursday at Amerant Bank Arena in Sunrise. The Panthers are 4-2-2 and the Canucks 2-6-1; Canucks Army describes the loss as a sixth straight. Seth Jones had two assists, and Akira Schmid made 15 saves. Liam Öhgren and defenceman Elias Pettersson scored for Vancouver, and Leevi Merilainen made 36 saves. Öhgren's goal, his second of the season, came at 7:23 on Vancouver's first shot; Pettersson's third of the year came at 17:05 off a pass from Filip Chytil, who was making his season debut after a shoulder injury. Tkachuk scored at 11:11 of the third, tied it with 12.8 seconds left after Florida pulled Schmid with 2:30 to go, and finished the hat trick — his second in two games, and his fifth in the NHL — at 2:23 of overtime. Canucks Army notes Vancouver killed both Florida power plays and has now gone two games without allowing a power-play goal. Before the game, general manager Ryan Johnson traded centre Aatu Räty to the Toronto Maple Leafs for forwards Jacob Quillan and Brandon Buhr; Buhr, 24, is a Burnaby product, and Quillan has three points in 24 NHL games. Scratches were Guillaume Brisebois, Luke Schenn, and Arshdeep Bains. The Canucks end a six-game road trip Saturday at 1 p.m. against the Tampa Bay Lightning. > **Thirteen point eight billion dollars is the deficit B.C.'s three main leaders debated Wednesday.**

**What You Need to Know:** Thirteen point eight billion dollars is the deficit B.C.'s three main leaders debated Wednesday, in the only televised debate before the October 24 election. Burnaby Schools now say files copied in the September ransomware attack may include medical information. A Washington grand jury has indicted an alleged co-conspirator in the Tumbler Ridge mass shooting.

### Top Stories
**Cyberattack may have leaked student and parent information, Burnaby school district says: The Globe and Mail**
The Burnaby School District says a ransomware attack on September 21 hit school websites and portals, internal network services and phone lines. In an online notice, the district says hackers copied and stole files that may have held lists of parent, guardian and student names and contact information, plus birthdates, grades and school names. The notice says the copied material may also include registration forms, kindergarten assessment notes and detailed lists of students on specialized learning plans. CBC reports the district now says the compromised material may include identifying documents and medical information, including medical diagnoses. The district says the RCMP and B.C.'s privacy commissioner have the matter, that system security is being evaluated, and that staff, students and families have been offered registration with TransUnion's fraud alert service. The notice asks people to be wary of suspicious communications and says the district will update the community as the investigation proceeds. Source: [theglobeandmail.com](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/canada/british-columbia/article-cyberattack-burnaby-school-district-student-parent-information/) Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/buranby-schools-cyberattack-update-9.7381425)

**Tax total for Canadian softwood lumber exports set at almost 35% after U.S. review: CBC**

**Alleged Tumbler Ridge shooting co-conspirator James Cody Bryant indicted by grand jury: CBC**
A grand jury in Washington state has indicted 30-year-old James Bryant, an alleged co-conspirator in the Tumbler Ridge, B.C., mass shooting. **'A model of courage:' Third victim of Tsawwassen Mills crash dies in hospital: Vancouver Sun**
A 64-year-old woman has died of injuries from the September 30 crash at Tsawwassen Mills, the Vancouver Sun reports. She is the third person to die from that crash. ### City & Province
**Vancouver Aquatic Centre 25-metre rebuild a First Nation’s land claim issue: Park Board chair: Global News**
Park Board chair Tom Digby, who is running for re-election as a Vancouver Green Party commissioner and was chair when the board decided to demolish the aging Vancouver Aquatic Centre, told Global News the centre cannot be rebuilt as a 50-metre pool because of unsettled land claims. The Park Board has said a 50-metre pool would need a larger footprint to meet modern safety and competition rules. Digby said the province owns the land and will not allow that expansion, mainly because land claims with First Nations on the foreshore are unsettled. Musqueam Chief Wayne Sparrow confirmed a request to expand the footprint and said the province sent a letter to MST Development Corporation, the partnership of the Musqueam Indian Band, Squamish Nation and Tsleil-Waututh Nation, wanting a lease to the city. Sparrow said the province was proposing to lease the land for as little as one dollar, and asked what Musqueam's accommodation would be. He said there has been no meeting yet with the province and MST, and that one could still happen. Protecting Our Vancouver Aquatic Centre won an interim injunction pausing demolition until at least November 3, the day after the first scheduled Park Board meeting. Group director and TEAM park board candidate Jon Girard said that if the facility is renovated or rebuilt, it needs to stay a 50-metre pool. First Nations in B.C. are calling on Ottawa to set national standards for Indigenous consultations on major projects. They say they were given limited time to review the proposal. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12102948/major-projects-office-bc-first-nations-frustrations/)

### The Closer Look
**B.C. Election: Eby, Doerkson and Lowan spar over economic vision in televised leader's debate: Vancouver Sun**
NDP Leader David Eby, Conservative interim leader Lorne Doerkson and Green Leader Emily Lowan debated for almost two hours Wednesday night in downtown Vancouver, in the only televised leaders' debate before the October 24 provincial election. Moderator Shachi Kurl, president of the Angus Reid Institute, led them through the topics. The Vancouver Sun reports the exchange was long on policy. Voting by mail has to be delivered by the October 17 deadline, a related note in that coverage says.

Eby was challenged at the outset for calling a snap election two years after the last vote, with his party holding a majority. He said that with a one-seat majority, appointing the speaker leaves the house tied, so every vote could bring down the government. He said this was not a government able to deliver the big swings families need, and that the province needs representatives from every part of B.C. focused on priorities, not culture wars or repealing the human rights code. Doerkson said the election is about Eby's decade in the legislature, that nothing is better than years ago, and that he will lead with respect and dignity and expect that from his caucus. He told CityNews he does not want to introduce a platform he breaks promises on. Lowan, described by one report as the youngest and only woman on the stage, said she is a renter who has done minimum-wage work, and that the Greens have a plan on the cost of living and climate through sustainability and community-driven growth. If the Greens held the balance of power, she said, her top priority would be a better voting system, which she located in proportional representation.

On the books, Eby cited hospitals and schools for the projected deficit and said he would address wasteful spending. He said spending had been essential and that the budget could be balanced without burdening residents. His plan, as the Sun reports it, would raise taxes on individuals making over one hundred ninety thousand dollars a year to fund expanded social services, and give a temporary break on the ten-cent-per-litre fuel tax. He attacked the Conservative plan to raise the amount people can earn before paying income tax to thirty-two thousand dollars, which some economists say could cost the treasury up to four billion dollars, and said Conservatives cut when they need money. Doerkson criticized spending, including a previously proposed one-thousand-dollar rebate that was retracted, and said he would supercharge the economy with that tax change, a tripling of LNG production by 2035, fewer regulations, and a temporary removal of the ten percent PST on Canadian liquor. He argued for forestry and LNG. Lowan said money was going into resource extraction without a sustainable path, and she wants value-added local industry. She proposed a tax on ultra-wealthy households to fund social services. Eby said he had created thousands of daycare spaces and that more progress is needed. On health care, Lowan said he had not met commitments on access to family doctors. Eby stressed recruiting professionals and pointed to demographic challenges ahead.

On ICBC, Doerkson proposed replacing the no-fault system with a hybrid model. Eby pointed to losses he said followed when personal-injury lawyers were in the system. On Indigenous rights, Eby reaffirmed partnership with Indigenous communities. Doerkson pledged to repeal the Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act, arguing it has bred division. Lowan defended the act and said the work is to realize it, not dismantle it.

Doerkson was asked about social-media reposts by campaign manager Katy Merrifield, including one calling Islam a literal rape culture and another calling New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani a Jihadi-loving mayor. He said she was reacting to events in the U.K. as a survivor of sexual assault, has apologized and deleted the reposts, and will stay. He has already removed one candidate over a post targeting pro-Palestinian protesters. Eby said her feed at points reads like the worst corners of the dark web, and that Doerkson was standing against a call from national Muslim organizations that people need to feel safe. Lowan said the exchange felt like the 2024 race, with a Conservative party divided by candidates' comments and what she called a managed decline under Eby. Asked if he could work with the Conservatives to avoid another election, Eby said he struggles to see common ground, that he is not perfect, and that he will act in the best interests of British Columbians.

CentreBC leader Elenore Sturko, in video remarks, said she is not asking voters to pretend CentreBC will form government, and asked who will hold the next government accountable. She called her party socially progressive, environmentally pragmatic and fiscally responsible. OneBC leader Dallas Brodie, also in video remarks, said her party will push a twenty-five percent income-tax cut for individuals and corporations, a two percent PST cut, and a fight against what she called land-back giveaways and the reconciliation industry. # Vancouver Daily News
> **Nearly 104,000 people have already voted ahead of Saturday's Vancouver civic election.**

**What You Need to Know:** Nearly 104,000 people have already voted ahead of Saturday's Vancouver civic election, after Tuesday set a single-day advance record. The B.C. Court of Appeal has paused demolition at the Vancouver Aquatic Centre until November 3. Tonight is the only scheduled provincial leaders' debate before the October 24 election.

### Top Stories
**Vancouver advance voting closes near 104,000 after four record days: Daily Hive**
The City of Vancouver's preliminary figures put advance turnout at 103,810 across four days. Tuesday, October 13, drew 29,096 voters, a new single-day early-voting record, after 21,824 on October 3, 25,142 on October 7 and 27,748 on October 10. Daily Hive reports that is about 60 per cent above roughly 65,000 advance voters in the 2022 civic election, and about 61 per cent of the 171,494 ballots cast in that entire election. Advance locations nearly tripled, from 22 to 59, while advance days fell from five to four. The City said voters reported quick visits despite the higher turnout. Main voting day is Saturday, October 17, with 85 locations open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m.; mail-in ballots must be at a designated drop-off by 8 p.m. that day to count. Voters choose a mayor, councillors, park board commissioners and school trustees, plus a capital-plan borrowing plebiscite and two non-binding public-safety questions on hard-drug enforcement in public and a secure treatment facility. Daily Hive says it is unclear whether the early surge will lift overall turnout. Source: [dailyhive.com](https://dailyhive.com/vancouver/vancouver-2026-civic-municipal-election-advance-voting-total-turnout)

**Appeal court pauses Vancouver Aquatic Centre demolition until November 3: Daily Hive**
B.C. Court of Appeal Justice Dickson has granted an interim injunction halting further demolition of the closed Vancouver Aquatic Centre until November 3, the day after the new park board's inaugural meeting on November 2. Protecting Our Vancouver Aquatic Centre Society and TEAM for a Livable Vancouver announced the order. It does not cancel the redevelopment, require a 50-metre pool, or overturn a September Supreme Court ruling that the City and park board could use $103 million in 2022 voter-approved borrowing for a 25-metre concept. Society director and TEAM park board candidate Jonathan Girard said interim injunctions are among the hardest orders to win, and that the court "made sure the people's representatives still get to decide." The order covers interior demolition, stripping, site preparation, and dismantling of the exterior, interior structures and pool basins. The City and park board may apply to allow hazardous-materials removal that would preserve the building, with two days' notice to the society. A $3.5-million demolition contract went to Heatherbrae Builders in July; the construction contract is not yet awarded. The City had aimed to start major work in late 2026 or early 2027 and open in 2029. The centre opened in 1974, closed June 28, 2026, and had been set for demolition on October 1. The approved concept is a $175-million complex with a 25-metre, eight-lane lap pool, leisure pool, diving pool, hot tub and gym. TEAM, ABC Vancouver and the Vancouver Liberals have promised a 50-metre pool at this Sunset Beach site; the Green Party of Vancouver, Vote Vancouver and OneCity have promised a 50-metre pool elsewhere in the city. Source: [dailyhive.com](https://dailyhive.com/vancouver/vancouver-aquatic-centre-demolition-pause-bc-appeal-court-decision)

**Only scheduled provincial leaders' debate is tonight: Global News**
The only scheduled leaders' debate before the October 24 provincial election is tonight, from 6:15 p.m. until 8 p.m. B.C. NDP leader David Eby, B.C. Conservative leader Lorne Doerkson and B.C. Green leader Emily Lowan are taking part. Shachi Kurl, president of the Angus Reid Institute, is the moderator. A live post-debate show with Keith Baldrey and Ben O'Hara-Byrne follows. Global News says the story will be updated during and after the debate. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12101213/watch-bc-election-provincial-leaders-debate-live/)

### City & Province
**Locke pressed on what she knew before the police chief's firing: Vancouver Sun**
Days before Surrey's election, mayoral candidate Mike Starchuk is pressing incumbent mayor Brenda Locke on the May 29 closed police-board meeting that moved to terminate then-chief Norm Lipinski. Starchuk said councillor Rob Stutt, of Locke's Surrey Connect party, chaired that meeting and should say whether he told Locke its purpose beforehand. "Either he talked to the mayor about that meeting or he didn't," Starchuk said. Surrey Connect said Locke has no involvement in human-resources matters and that Surrey Police Service staff decisions are made by the police board, independent of the city and the mayor. At a CKNW debate last week, Locke said she knew the board had an important meeting that day and, asked if she knew what was in it, answered, "Not really." Starchuk said that is not a no. Surrey First's Linda Annis said that if elected she will carry out an anti-corruption review, citing resident questions about land purchases, stop-work orders and Lipinski's termination before the RCMP transition was complete. Lipinski was chief from 2020 until June, when the board ended his contract without cause; the board had been in place fewer than 10 weeks. His contract had been renewed in October 2025 for three years, with an option for two more. Board chair Harley Chappell was not at the termination meeting. Late last month Lipinski asked the B.C. Supreme Court to quash the firing as unlawful and motivated by extraneous political considerations. None of those allegations has been tested in court, and no response had been filed as of Tuesday. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/incumbent-mayor-brenda-locke-under-renewed-scrutiny-over-termination-of-surrey-police-chief)

**Judge dismisses NDP petition over Vancouver-Yaletown nominations: Vancouver Sun**
A B.C. Supreme Court judge on Tuesday dismissed a B.C. NDP petition that questioned the legitimacy of at least one candidate in Vancouver-Yaletown. The petition alleged nomination forms for two candidates contained questionable names and signatures. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/judge-dismisses-bc-ndp-challenge-green-candidate-yaletown)

### The Closer Look
**Surrey firefighters win Muscular Dystrophy Canada's fire department award: Fire & Safety Journal Americas**
Sixty Surrey firefighters raised $25,000 for Muscular Dystrophy Canada this year, and that work has now drawn a national award. Fire & Safety Journal Americas reports the campaign lifted Surrey Local 1271's lifetime contribution to the charity to $266,000 and earned the Surrey Fire Fighters Charitable Society the 2026 Dr. David Green Award for Fire Department of the Year. The award will be presented to the local at a ceremony in Ottawa in November.

The fundraising is an annual boot-toll drive. Typically over a long weekend, firefighters volunteering with Local 1271's charitable society spread across 20 locations in Surrey and collect at busy commercial sites. Local 1271 president Mike Vincent said the recognition mattered to members and their families. "It hits home with our members," Vincent said. "They bring out their families and their kids and they engage the community. It's not easy asking for money with the way inflation is these days, but once people see you're a firefighter, they're just glad to come by and drop off a donation."

John Watkins, a Local 1271 member who also serves with the charitable society, tied the award to the job itself. "We do this work in the community because we made a commitment to help others when we signed up for this job," Watkins said. "This award is really a testament to the commitment of our members."

The Dr. David Green Awards recognize people and organizations whose dedication has had a lasting impact on Canadians living with neuromuscular disorders. Green, a neurologist, researcher and advocate, co-founded Muscular Dystrophy Canada in 1954 with Arthur Minden and pushed for better care, research, awareness and inclusion. Chief executive Stacey Lintern said Surrey firefighters "lead by example" and have encouraged other British Columbia affiliates of the International Association of Fire Fighters to support the charity. "We're deeply grateful for their partnership in breaking down barriers for people living with neuromuscular disorders, helping expand access to support, strengthen community connections and advance research as we continue the search for cures," Lintern said. Sixth District vice president Mike Carter called the award "a tremendous honor" and a reflection of what those members can do in their communities, and of the union's partnership with the charity.

The same charitable society delivers food to approximately 75 schools, awards student bursaries and has provided around 400 refurbished laptops to local students. Affiliates across the union raised $1.1 million for Muscular Dystrophy Canada last year through boot tolls, rooftop campouts and other community drives. ### Both Sides: Downtown office vacancy
The question in a Vancouver Sun report is whether downtown Vancouver's office market is recovering with other Canadian downtowns. The reading on offer is an assessment the paper publishes, not a council vote. Its best reason is the direction of the change: those downtowns, it says, are no longer stuck and have begun to improve. The strongest case that Vancouver is outside that recovery is the exception in the same assessment. It says Vancouver has not turned the corner, and it calls the difference highly unusual. That is the reason it offers for treating this core differently from the others. The fact that reading treats as common ground is the yardstick: downtown vacancy, compared city by city. ### Top Stories
**Whitecaps draw LAFC and clinch a playoff spot: Indo-Canadian Voice**
The Vancouver Whitecaps drew Los Angeles FC 1-1. Oliver Larraz scored his first goal. The club played with 10 men and clinched a berth in the Audi 2026 MLS Cup Playoffs. A Vancouver Sun video has incumbent mayor Ken Sim talking about zero per cent property taxes and business certainty. In the same video he also talks about affordability and public safety. What is being decided is the calendar in front of B.C. voters. CBC reports that candidates say overlapping elections are causing confusion. On October 17, voters elect mayors, councillors, school board trustees and other local officials. On October 24, a provincial vote elects 93 members of the legislature, which will determine B.C.’s next premier. Global News reports the same two dates and describes the dual elections as a headache for some B.C. voters.

The strongest case that the overlap is a problem comes from those candidates. Their reason, as CBC reports it, is that people are being asked to track two elections at once, for different offices, seven days apart. Global News puts that cost on voters who are already finding the pair of dates a headache, with local offices one week and the legislature the next.

Vaughn Palmer reports in the Vancouver Sun that the B.C. NDP leader sidestepped repeated questions about election timing. # Vancouver Daily News
> **More than twenty thousand homes lost power Friday as winds hit the Lower Mainland.**

**What You Need to Know:** Friday's winds knocked out power for more than twenty thousand households in the Lower Mainland and on the Sunshine Coast and delayed B.C. Ferries sailings. The Canada Border Services Agency has changed hours at nine land crossings so they match U.S. ports after B.C. ended seasonal time changes. The B.C. Lions clinched a playoff spot with a 41-20 win over Ottawa.

### Top Stories
**Strong winds topple trees and cut power: Vancouver Sun**
More than 20,000 households in the Lower Mainland and on the Sunshine Coast were without power Friday after strong winds, the Vancouver Sun reports. CBC News says those winds pummeled the Lower Mainland and toppled trees. The same winds delayed B.C. Ferries sailings, the Sun reports. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/local-news/winds-cause-power-outages-for-thousands-delay-bc-ferries) · [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/lower-mainland-windstorm-power-outage-damage-9.7376969?cmp=rss)

**Border hours change at nine land crossings: CBC News**
British Columbia's decision to end seasonal time changes has prompted the Canada Border Services Agency to alter opening hours at nine land crossings. CBC News reports the change is meant to align those crossings with neighbouring U.S. ports of entry. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/bc-border-crossing-hours-time-change-9.7377028?cmp=rss)

**Seatbelt and distracted-driving tickets double in a blitz: CBC News**
The British Columbia Highway Patrol says a recent enforcement blitz found an alarming increase in people driving distracted and not wearing seatbelts. CBC News reports the number of tickets doubled. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/distracted-driving-seatbelt-tickets-9.7376896?cmp=rss)

**Bayside Lounge to close after 47 years: Global News**
The Bayside Lounge, a West End staple that has supported local musicians and artists and welcomed visitors from around the world, is closing after 47 years as costs rise, Global News reports. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12097979/vancouver-bayside-lounge-closing/)

### City & Province
**RCMP ask for help naming a Surrey fraud suspect: CityNews**
The RCMP Surrey Provincial Operations Support Unit is asking the public to help identify a suspect in an alleged fraud. On September 22, around 9:18 a.m., police were called to a home in Fleetwood. The victim told investigators the suspect had come the evening before to buy his black 2018 Ford F-150, and alleges he was given a fake bank draft and shown fake identification. Police describe the suspect as a man about 30, five foot eight, medium build, in a green shirt and black pants. Anyone with information is asked to call Surrey Police Services at 604-599-0502 and cite file 26-29409 (SU). Source: [vancouver.citynews.ca](https://vancouver.citynews.ca/2026/10/09/surrey-fraud-suspect/)

**Conservatives promise seniors measures on the trail: Global News**
Global News reports B.C. leaders spent October 9 on the campaign trail talking about health care and support for seniors. The Conservatives are promising a series of measures, including reversing the NDP's changes to the property-tax deferment program and building more long-term-care beds. Those are campaign promises, not enacted policy. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12097726/bc-leaders-campaign-trail-health-care-supporting-seniors-october-9/)

### Getting Around

### Sports
**B.C. Lions clinch with a 41-20 win: Nanaimo News Now**
The B.C. Lions clinched a Grey Cup playoff spot, their fifth straight, with a 41-20 win over the Ottawa Redblacks on Friday at Save-On-Foods Field at BC Place in front of 22,083 fans. The win moved B.C. to 10-6, a ninth victory in ten games after a 1-5 start, and dropped Ottawa to 0-16. Nathan Rourke completed 25 of 31 passes for 360 yards, three touchdowns and one interception. Zander Horvath scored his 20th and 21st touchdowns of the season. Mathieu Betts called the clinch step one, with two weeks to chase the best seed possible. Source: [nanaimonewsnow.com](https://nanaimonewsnow.com/2026/10/09/b-c-lions-secure-playoff-spot-with-41-20-decision-over-winless-ottawa-redblacks/) · [bclions.com](https://bclions.com/article/bakes-game-takes-bc-ott-oct-9) · [cfl.ca](https://www.cfl.ca/article/bc-lions-clinch-postseason-berth-with-win-on-mobil-thanksgiving-weekend)

### Both Sides: Water conservation before a strong El Niño
Advocates want the next British Columbia government to strengthen water conservation because a forecast super El Niño could worsen drought. The World Meteorological Organization said Thursday that sea-surface temperatures in the central and eastern tropical Pacific are forecast to reach record levels, peaking in December. Secretary-General Celeste Saulo said El Niño is firmly established and strengthening rapidly, with a near-100 per cent likelihood it persists through February 2027, potentially one of the strongest since at least 1950.

Coree Tull, chair of the B.C. Watershed Coalition, says that pattern should bring a milder winter, more rain, less mountain snowpack and a smaller spring melt. She says many watersheds are carrying a long-term deficit into 2027, so another thin snow year could compound drought already here. She names possible next-summer impacts as more water restrictions, higher costs for communities and farmers, critically low flows for fish and other wildlife, and increased wildfire fuels. River Forecast Centre data cited with those comments show high-level drought in B.C. every year since 2015, including more widespread severe drought from 2022 to 2024.

This week's Drought and Water Scarcity Bulletin says recent precipitation has improved conditions across the province. It also says Okanagan streamflow remained concerningly low, and that communities on southeast Vancouver Island and in the Thompson-Okanagan still face concerns about drinking water. Tull and the bulletin both treat the drought as multi-year, and both treat those regions as still under stress. The dated marker in the forecast is the WMO window through February 2027. Source: [mybulkleylakesnow.com](https://www.mybulkleylakesnow.com/advocates-urge-next-b-c-government-to-address-water-scarcity-as-el-nino-forecast-adds-to-drought-concerns/)

# Vancouver Daily News
> **One point separates Fry and Sim for Vancouver mayor, inside the poll's margin.**

**What You Need to Know:** A Canada Pulse Insights poll for CityNews and OMNI puts Green candidate Pete Fry at 28 per cent and incumbent Ken Sim at 27 per cent among decided voters, inside a margin of plus or minus 4.4 points, with Vancouver's election just over a week away. Victoria-Beacon Hill candidate Joachim Agou, dropped by the B.C. Conservatives, has apologized and says he will run as an independent on October 24. Former attorney general Colin Gablemann has died at 82.

### Top Stories
**One point splits Fry and Sim in a CityNews mayor poll: CityNews Vancouver:**
With Vancouver's municipal election just over a week away, a Canada Pulse Insights poll done exclusively for CityNews and OMNI puts Green Party candidate Pete Fry at 28 per cent and incumbent Ken Sim at 27 per cent among decided voters, inside a margin of error of plus or minus 4.4 percentage points. Vancouver Liberal candidate Kareem Allam is at 19 per cent. Among decided voters who say they will definitely vote or have already cast a ballot, Fry is at 29 per cent and Sim at 28. Among decided voters, TEAM for a Livable Vancouver's Colleen Hardwick is at 13 per cent, Vote Vancouver's Rebecca Bligh at seven, and Bright Future Vancouver's Muhammad Ahmad at three. John Wright, CEO of Canada Pulse Insights, calls the field very fragmented, with two front-runners and two streams: he says Fry's supporters emphasize the environment, ethics, accountability, affordability and housing, while Sim's emphasize affordability first, then crime, municipal taxes and the bottom line. Ten per cent of all respondents were still undecided after people who first said they were unsure were asked if they were leaning. Wright says a typical campaign has about 18 to 20 per cent undecided, with 10 per cent who will not show up, and that the remaining share is often weighing personalities. Source: [vancouver.citynews.ca](https://vancouver.citynews.ca/2026/10/09/vancouver-mayoral-race-a-dead-heat-between-fry-and-sim-poll/)

**Dropped Conservative candidate Joachim Agou apologizes, will run as an independent: Global BC:**
Victoria-Beacon Hill candidate Joachim Agou, removed from the B.C. Conservatives over online posts the NDP called racist, says he is truly sorry, takes responsibility for his words, and rejects any accusation of racism. In one post he said a car that drove through a pro-Palestine protest "should have reversed" over demonstrators; in another he shared a meme that used an expletive to describe Pakistan. Interim Conservative leader Lorne Doerkson said the posts are inexcusable and that, if Agou is elected October 24, he will not be part of the Conservative caucus. Agou says he should have expressed himself "more clearly and calmly," and that such demonstrations "should not bring a city to a standstill or put lives at risk." He says he understands why the party withdrew support and will run as an independent in a riding considered an NDP stronghold. CBC reports the Conservatives dropped him Thursday and that he still plans to run. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12097012/bc-joachim-agou-apologizes/) · [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/b-c-conservatives-drop-candidate-for-victoria-beacon-hill-after-offensive-social-media-posts-9.7374798?cmp=rss)

**Former attorney general Colin Gablemann dies at 82: CBC British Columbia:**
Colin Gablemann, a former British Columbia attorney general who played a key role in the province's freedom-of-information laws and in recognizing Indigenous rights, has died at 82. CBC describes him as transformative. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/colin-gablemann-former-attorney-general-9.7375206?cmp=rss)

**Squamish woman pleads guilty to terrorism charge: Vancouver Sun:**
Kimberly Polman, a Squamish woman who wed an ISIS fighter, pleaded guilty to participating in ISIS about a month before her trial was expected to start in B.C. Supreme Court, after days of pretrial hearings that included Charter challenges. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/squamish-woman-who-wed-isis-fighter-pleads-guilty-in-bc-to-terrorism-charge)

### City & Province
**NDP promises a three-year freeze on ICBC rates if elected: Global BC:**
The B.C. NDP is promising to freeze car insurance rates for three years if elected. NDP Leader David Eby and interim B.C. Conservative leader Lorne Doerkson traded barbs about the future of the no-fault insurance model, which the B.C. NDP introduced in 2021. The pledge is a campaign promise, not a rate decision in force. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12092908/bc-ndp-bc-conservatives-icbc-rates/)

**Sooke infrastructure sits at the centre of its municipal election: CBC British Columbia:**
In the District of Sooke on Vancouver Island, population has grown steadily since the early 2000s, and local infrastructure has struggled to keep pace because of environmental regulations and a growing strain on limited resources. CBC reports that infrastructure is set to play a key role in the municipal election there. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/sooke-infrastructure-plays-key-role-municipal-elections-9.7370362?cmp=rss)

### Getting Around
DriveBC lists night paving on Highway 1A in Surrey from October 16 to 19, 9 p.m. on the 16th to 5 a.m. on the 19th: a northbound lane closed, the southbound exit to King George Boulevard closed, and a detour via the Highway 17 westbound off-ramp, Tannery Road, 120 Street and King George Boulevard. On Highway 99 in Vancouver, paving from October 14 to 16 runs 11 p.m. to 5 a.m. Wednesday and Thursday, with single-lane alternating traffic northbound and southbound open only to buses and emergency vehicles. In Delta, the Highway 99 Exit 23 ramp to Ladner Trunk Road stays closed through October 23, and night work from Ladner Trunk Road to Highway 17 runs to October 18, 9 p.m. to 5 a.m. Monday to Saturday, with one lane each way. Environment Canada has no watches or warnings for Vancouver: Friday showers end this morning, then sun and cloud, northwest wind 30 km/h gusting to 50, and to 70 near the Strait of Georgia, high 15, UV index 3. Friday night is partly cloudy with a 60 per cent chance of showers and a low of 9; Saturday is cloudy with a 60 per cent chance of early showers, clearing near noon, high 16; Sunday is sunny, high 16. Source: [drivebc.ca](https://www.drivebc.ca/) · [weather.gc.ca](https://weather.gc.ca/rss/weather/49.245_-123.115_e.xml)

### Both Sides: Tax promises against a $13.8-billion deficit
British Columbians are being asked, in the first half of the provincial campaign, to choose among promises to hold, hike or cut taxes. Global News reports that whoever becomes premier will face a projected deficit of about $13.8 billion. These are campaign promises, not measures now in law. The vote is October 24.

NDP Leader David Eby's case for changing the tax mix is that services such as health care have to be paid for. He is proposing to suspend gasoline taxes, add a bracket for people making more than $1 million, and increase taxes on the two highest existing income brackets, which start at about $190,000. Eby has said those changes would generate $1 billion.

The Conservative case for cutting taxes is that the economy needs a jolt. Interim leader Lorne Doerkson is promising no new taxes, elimination of the PST on some items, and a $1,000 cut in provincial taxes for nearly every working British Columbian. He argues the cuts are needed to "supercharge" an economy that lost 26,000 jobs in August. The Conservatives say increasing taxes will drive away doctors.

Green Leader Emily Lowan's case is that extreme wealth should fund public services through a one-time "fair share tax": five per cent on net wealth above $50 million, 10 per cent above $100 million, and 20 per cent above $1 billion. The party estimates that would raise about $22.2 billion. Lowan has criticized Eby for co-opting "the language of the left" after, she said, he refused her extreme-wealth-tax proposal while he was in power.

The shared fiscal frame in the reporting is that projected deficit of about $13.8 billion. No party in the article has turned a promise into a passed budget. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12096989/bc-election-take-on-taxes/)

# Vancouver Daily News
> **More than twenty-five thousand advance ballots set a one-day record in Vancouver's municipal election.**

**What You Need to Know:** Vancouver’s Wednesday advance vote broke the city’s single-day record, with more than 25,000 ballots cast. Average asking rent in B.C. fell 2.9 percent in September, a second straight year of annual declines. A yellow fog advisory is up for Vancouver, two West Vancouver exit ramps were closed overnight, and the Highway 99 exit to Ladner Trunk Road stays shut.

### Top Stories
**Vancouver sets a single-day advance-voting record: CBC British Columbia**
After a record opening day of advance voting, Wednesday went further. CBC British Columbia reports that Vancouver voters set a new single-day early-voting record in the municipal election, with more than 25,000 advance ballots cast. **B.C. asking rents fall for a second year: CBC British Columbia**
Average asking rent in British Columbia fell 2.9 percent in September, CBC British Columbia reports, citing a monthly report from Rentals.ca and Urbanation. That report said the figures mark two full years of annual declines, the longest downturn the Canadian rental market has experienced in recent history. Three horses were killed and a fourth was injured in a crash on a B.C. highway, CBC British Columbia reports. **Crown seeks two years in a stroller hit-and-run: Global BC**
Crown prosecutors are seeking a two-year jail term for Kyle Nicholas Luca, 31, Global BC reports. The B.C. Conservatives are spending a second straight day campaigning in Surrey, which NanaimoNewsNOW describes as a critical battleground, and interim leader Lorne Doerkson is there to make a policy announcement. **Canucks visit the Hurricanes tonight: Fubo**
The Vancouver Canucks play the Carolina Hurricanes tonight at 7 p.m. Eastern at Lenovo Center in Raleigh, on the Hurricanes Hockey Network, Fubo reports. Carolina, the defending Stanley Cup champion, is 2-1-1 with five points; Vancouver is 2-2-0 with four. Sebastian Aho has four goals and three assists in four games. It says Carolina is likely to start Pyotr Kochetkov, at 1.91 and .889. ### Both Sides: A provincial inquiry into the North Shore sewage plant
The decision in front of the provincial government is whether to open its own inquiry into the North Shore Wastewater Treatment Plant. Daily Hive reports the construction budget has risen from 700 million dollars to 3.9 billion, and the construction timeline has been extended by a decade.

City of North Vancouver mayor Linda Buchanan and District of North Vancouver mayor Mike Little want the province to commission an independent inquiry into the plant, and a broader review of how Metro Vancouver manages multibillion-dollar capital projects. Their case starts with the households they represent: their municipalities are among those most affected by the cost increases and by the pressure those increases put on household bills. They are asking for scrutiny that is not limited to a review ordered by the regional government running the project.

Metro Vancouver’s case is that a review is already underway. The regional government has commissioned an independent review and is already examining the escalating costs and the oversight, with findings expected by January 2027. It argues that commissioning another review would create an unnecessary cost for taxpayers. In the same response to election criticism, board chair Mike Hurley, mayor of Burnaby, said claims that Metro Vancouver is out of control rely on outdated or untrue information. The district says less than eight percent of its operating budget goes to non-utility services, and that the Iona Island plant estimate has been cut from 9.9 billion dollars to 6 billion.

Both sides are working from the same overrun: 700 million dollars became 3.9 billion, and the build gained a decade. The dated next step on the books is the regional review’s findings in January 2027. A separate provincial inquiry would be a decision for the provincial government. Source: [dailyhive.com](https://dailyhive.com/vancouver/metro-vancouver-regional-district-bc-conservatives-platform-response)

# Vancouver Daily News
> **A fifty-thousand-dollar penalty hits LNG Canada over underwater noise at its tug terminal.**

**What You Need to Know:** LNG Canada has been handed a fifty-thousand-dollar administrative penalty tied to underwater noise while a North Coast tug terminal was built. Seasonal illness is rising earlier than usual, and the province is set to set out immunization plans. Eastbound Highway 1 at Kensington has reopened after a death investigation, and a yellow fog advisory is in effect for Vancouver this morning.

### Top Stories
**LNG Canada fined $50,000 over underwater noise monitoring: CBC British Columbia**
The company behind a major LNG export terminal on British Columbia's North Coast has been handed a fifty-thousand-dollar administrative penalty. The penalty relates to underwater noise while a tug terminal was being built three years ago. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/lng-canada-fine-underwater-noise-monitoring-9.7371937?cmp=rss)

**B.C. set to announce immunization plans amid an early flu peak: CBC British Columbia**
The B.C. Centre for Disease Control says seasonal illnesses are on the rise earlier than usual this year. The province is set to announce immunization plans. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/province-immunizations-early-peak-flu-season-9.7371820?cmp=rss)

**Police investigating after a man's body was found on Highway 1 in Burnaby: CityNews Vancouver**
Burnaby RCMP says it is investigating after a man's body was found lying in the eastbound lanes of Highway 1 just east of Kensington on Monday morning. Officers were called shortly before 6 a.m. Mounties said the man was obviously deceased and had injuries consistent with being hit by a vehicle. Police closed all eastbound lanes so evidence could be preserved; the lanes stayed closed for more than twelve hours and have since reopened. Mounties say it is possible the man was killed by a vehicle that then left the scene. BC Highway Patrol Sgt. Michael McLaughlin said officers are investigating all possibilities and asked anyone who saw anything unusual near Kensington between 5:30 a.m. and 6 a.m. to call, including dash-cam video that may not show a collision, at 604-526-9744. Source: [vancouver.citynews.ca](https://vancouver.citynews.ca/2026/10/06/highway-1-burnaby-closed-eastbound-incident/)

**BC Greens propose a wealth tax on fortunes over $50 million: Daily Hive Vancouver**
BC Greens leader Emily Lowan announced a proposed Fair Share Act ahead of the October 24 provincial election. The party says it would apply a one-time tax on net wealth above fifty million dollars, at five percent above that line, ten percent above one hundred million, and twenty percent above one billion, then an annual tax from the second year of two percent, three percent, and five percent at those same thresholds. Lowan says the money would support universal childcare, free public transit, and affordable housing, and would also pay down provincial debt. The party estimates twenty-two point two billion dollars in the first year and five point four billion dollars a year after that, and says the estimate accounts for administrative costs and changes in taxpayer behaviour. Lowan said families keep hearing that the money is not there, and that it sits with people who make more in their sleep than a worker makes in a year. Daily Hive reports that critics call the rates excessive, a deterrent to investment, and a risk that some households would owe large bills without cash on hand. Source: [dailyhive.com](https://dailyhive.com/vancouver/bc-greens-wealth-tax-fair-share-act)

### City & Province
**B.C. Conservatives say they would allow lawsuits over vehicle accidents: CBC British Columbia**
B.C. Conservative Leader Lorne Doerkson says his party would replace no-fault insurance with a hybrid system that would once again allow lawsuits, according to a leaked letter. That is a campaign proposal, not a change in law. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/bc-conservatives-no-fault-insurance-9.7372057?cmp=rss)

**North Vancouver's Grouse Grind closing for four weeks: North Shore News**
Metro Vancouver is shutting the Grouse Grind on October 13 for annual maintenance. A reopening is planned for November 10, weather permitting. Source: [nsnews.com](https://www.nsnews.com/local-news/north-vancouvers-grouse-grind-closing-for-four-weeks-for-annual-maintenance-12859629)

**B.C. union launches a petition on the film tax credit: Vancouver Sun**
A petition backed by IATSE Local 891 is calling on Ottawa to change how the Production Services Tax Credit is calculated. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/bc-union-petition-seeking-film-tax-credit-change)

**Eby says the campaign focus is now affordability: NanaimoNewsNOW**
NDP Leader David Eby called the snap election on September 22 and said British Columbia needed a firebreak against Donald Trump's tariffs and what he called Trump-style politics. He now says the campaign has moved to affordability, and that he accepts not everyone shares his anxieties about the U.S. president, even as he says Trump's actions make B.C.'s challenges worse. He says the question for voters on October 24 is which party can support families. Source: [nanaimonewsnow.com](https://nanaimonewsnow.com/2026/10/07/b-c-ndp-leader-eby-says-not-everybody-shares-his-concerns-about-trump/)

**Squamish mayoral candidates clash in a watched debate: CBC British Columbia**
More than eight hundred people watched a Squamish mayoral debate ahead of the October 17 municipal election. Candidates clashed over property taxes and encampments. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/squamish-municipal-mayoral-debate-9.7371807?cmp=rss)

### Getting Around
A yellow fog advisory is in effect for Vancouver, issued at 4:56 a.m. Conditions were fog and 10.2 degrees. Fog is expected to dissipate this morning, then mainly sunny, with a high of 17 except 21 inland; tonight is clear, becoming partly cloudy, with fog patches near midnight and a low of 10. Thursday is mainly sunny after morning fog patches, high 18 except 22 inland. On the roads, the Highway 99 exit ramp at Exit 23 to Ladner Trunk Road in Delta stays closed all day until October 23. Dollarton Highway on-ramps, eastbound and westbound, were closed overnight until 6 a.m. today, with detours via Riverside Drive, Mount Seymour Parkway and Keith Road eastbound, and via Main Street, Brooksbank Avenue and the Mountain Highway interchange westbound. Westport Road and Headland Drive ramps in West Vancouver had overnight paving closures through 6 a.m. today. Night work on Highway 99 in Delta, from Ladner Trunk Road to Highway 17, runs 9 p.m. to 5 a.m. through October 18, with one lane open each way. A detour remains in effect on 264 Street in Langley until October 17. Source: [weather.gc.ca](https://weather.gc.ca/rss/weather/49.245_-123.115_e.xml) Source: [drivebc.ca](https://www.drivebc.ca/)

### Sports
**Chicago Fire 3, Vancouver Whitecaps 1: TSN**
Chicago Fire FC beat the Vancouver Whitecaps 3-1, with goals from three different scorers. It was Chicago's second victory in a row. Source: [tsn.ca](https://www.tsn.ca/soccer/video/2026/10/07/mls-fire-3-whitecaps-1/) Source: [chicagofirefc.com](https://www.chicagofirefc.com/news/match-recap-chicago-fire-fc-earns-second-victory-in-a-row-against-vancouver-whitecaps-fc)

**Hurricanes host the Canucks after Hall's two-goal game: FOX Sports**
The Vancouver Canucks, at 2-2, visit the Carolina Hurricanes, at 2-1-1, in Raleigh on Thursday at 7 p.m. Eastern. Taylor Hall scored two goals in Carolina's 6-4 win over Montreal. Thatcher Demko is out with a hip injury, Filip Chytil is out with a shoulder injury, and Akil Thomas, Mackenzie MacEachern and Jack Thompson are out with undisclosed injuries. Carolina's Seth Jarvis is out with a shoulder injury. Source: [foxsports.com](https://www.foxsports.com/articles/nhl/hurricanes-host-the-canucks-after-halls-2goal-game)

### What's On
**Coast Mountain Film Fest returns to the Rio Theatre: Vancouver Is Awesome**
The Coast Mountain Film Fest is at Vancouver's Rio Theatre on Thursday, November 5. Ski Night starts at 7 p.m. with Inside the Season, filmed in places including Whistler and Pemberton, plus the short The Way of Snow, which features two Whistler athletes. Snowboard Night at 9:30 p.m. includes a fifteenth-anniversary screening of CapiTA: Defenders of Awesome, originally released in 2011, plus 2026-season shorts. Tickets are on sale through the Rio Theatre site. Source: [vancouverisawesome.com](https://www.vancouverisawesome.com/events-and-entertainment/coast-mountain-film-fest-2026-12850844)

### Both Sides: A local role on Pacific Link
Prime Minister Mark Carney has designated the proposed Pacific Link oil pipeline a project of national interest. It would carry an additional one million barrels of Alberta oil a day toward a possible marine export terminal at Roberts Bank in Tsawwassen, largely following the existing Trans Mountain corridor into the eastern Lower Mainland. Ottawa is aiming to finalize the conditions needed to proceed by September 2027, while proponents work on route planning, environmental studies, cost estimates, and public and Indigenous consultations. The civic election is Saturday, October 17.

Vancouver Mayor Ken Sim, of ABC Vancouver, says his party supports projects that expand access to overseas markets, attract investment, and cut reliance on any single trading partner. He calls the pipeline a federal matter, says it would not pass through Vancouver, and says the city will not hire lawyers to try to block it. Surrey Mayor Brenda Locke, of Surrey Connect, calls the designation an important step toward diversifying energy exports, creating jobs, and strengthening economic sovereignty, and she points to meaningful Indigenous ownership and a focus on Canadian workers and materials.

Delta Mayor George Harvie, running again with Achieving For Delta, says these projects are significant economic opportunities and that Delta's job is to have a seat at the table and to understand benefits and potential harm together, including Vancouver Fraser Port Authority's separate Roberts Bank Terminal 2. He points to combined pressure on truck and train traffic, roads, transit, public services, farmland, and the environment, and says that stance is not anti-development. Tsawwassen First Nation has said it wants to be consulted directly because of possible impacts on its lands. All three mayors have welcomed the prospect of investment and jobs. Source: [dailyhive.com](https://dailyhive.com/vancouver/metro-vancouver-mayors-pacific-link-pipeline-support)

# Vancouver Daily News
> **96.9 percent of Vancouver school support workers voted to authorize strike action.**

**What You Need to Know:** Vancouver school support workers have given their union a strike mandate. Party leaders will meet in a televised debate on Oct. 14, and Monday’s health-care campaign stops put long-term care restarts beside a rural emergency-care fund. The B.C. Conservatives also say they would cut Metro Vancouver Regional District back to water and sewage.

### Top Stories
**Vancouver school support workers vote overwhelmingly to back strike action: CBC British Columbia**
The International Union of Operating Engineers Local 963 says members voted 96.9 percent in support of a strike mandate. The vote covers support workers at the Vancouver School Board. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/vsb-support-workers-strike-vote-9.7370385?cmp=rss)

**B.C. provincial leaders’ debate set for Oct. 14: Global BC**
The only live, streamed and televised leaders’ debate of the provincial campaign is set for Wednesday, Oct. 14, from 6:15 p.m. to 8 p.m., Global BC and CBC report. B.C. NDP Leader David Eby, B.C. Conservative Leader Lorne Doerkson and B.C. Green Party Leader Emily Lowan will take part. Shachi Kurl, president of the Angus Reid Institute, will moderate. The B.C. Broadcast Consortium — Global BC, CBC, CTV, Citytv and CHEK — is carrying it. Final voting day is Oct. 24. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12088589/bc-election-provincial-leaders-debate-2026/) https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/bc-provincial-election-leaders-debate-9.7370415?cmp=rss

**B.C. NDP and Conservatives set out health-care promises: My Nelson Now**
NDP Leader David Eby, speaking Monday at the Victoria Curling Club, said a re-elected NDP would resume seven long-term care projects the February budget paused indefinitely, in Abbotsford, Campbell River, Chilliwack, Delta, Fort St. John, Kelowna and Squamish. The 2026 budget put the cost to complete them at close to $1.4 billion. The NDP said the money would come from a partnership agreement B.C. and Ottawa reached in July. Eby also pledged funding for 500 additional health-care workers for at-home care, and a free shingles vaccine for everyone over 50 and all immunocompromised adults. The vaccine typically takes two doses, at about $150 a shot. The same day in 100 Mile House, Interim Leader Lorne Doerkson said a Conservative government would set up a $50 million emergency fund to help prevent emergency-room and maternity closures and to aid recruitment to rural practices, and would launch an expert review panel within 100 days to identify practices from other universal, publicly funded systems that could be used in B.C. Final voting day is Oct. 24. Source: [mynelsonnow.com](https://www.mynelsonnow.com/80690/news/elections/2026-bc-election/b-c-ndp-plans-to-resume-seven-paused-long-term-care-projects-if-re-elected/)

### City & Province
**Warning issued after 12-year-old Port Moody boy struck in face with firework: CBC British Columbia**
Port Moody police have issued a warning after a 12-year-old boy was struck in the face with a firework on Friday. Police and firefighters across Metro Vancouver typically see more firework calls in the run-up to Halloween. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/port-moody-12-year-old-firework-warning-9.7370226?cmp=rss) https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/port-moody-12-year-old-firework-warning-9.7370226

**Jewelry stolen from a Vancouver open house recovered by police: Vancouver Sun**
Two men were arrested after their vehicle was stopped. A search uncovered thousands of dollars of stolen jewelry taken from a Vancouver open house. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/jewelry-stolen-from-vancouver-open-house-recovered-by-police)

**Ontario man sentenced after YVR cannabis seizure: Vancouver Sun**
Alaaddin Koc, 56, was sentenced to a year in jail. Canada Border Services Agency officers intercepted him at Vancouver airport on Oct. 28, 2024, as he tried to fly to England with 31 kilos of cannabis. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/yvr-pot-smuggler-sentenced-year-jail)

### Getting Around
No weather watches or warnings are in effect. DriveBC says the Highway 99 exit ramp at Exit 23 to Ladner Trunk Road in Delta is closed all day, every day, from Tuesday, Oct. 6, through Friday, Oct. 23. Tonight, Tuesday, the eastbound and westbound Dollarton Highway on-ramps are closed from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m.; eastbound traffic is detoured via Riverside Drive to Mount Seymour Parkway to the Keith Road interchange, and westbound traffic via Main Street to Brooksbank Avenue to the Mountain Highway interchange. In West Vancouver, paving keeps the Westport Road ramps closed into Wednesday morning, from 9:30 a.m. to 6 a.m. the next day on Monday and Tuesday, and the Headland Drive ramps closed from 9:30 p.m. to 6 a.m. on the same nights. Night work on Highway 99 in Delta, from Ladner Trunk Road to Highway 17, runs to Sunday, Oct. 18, from 9 p.m. to 5 a.m., Monday to Saturday, with one lane open each way. Environment Canada’s Vancouver forecast: mist and 11.7 degrees this morning; Tuesday mainly cloudy, a 30 percent chance of drizzle early, clearing this afternoon, fog patches gone late morning, wind becoming west at 20 km/h, high 17 except 21 inland; Tuesday night low 10; Wednesday high 17 except 21 inland, low 10; Thursday sunny, high 18 except 22 inland. Source: [drivebc.ca](https://www.drivebc.ca/) https://weather.gc.ca/rss/weather/49.245_-123.115_e.xml

### Both Sides: Narrowing Metro Vancouver to water and sewage
Voters are being asked, in a Conservative platform promise, whether Metro Vancouver Regional District should be cut back to drinking water and sewage. Lorne Doerkson’s B.C. Conservatives say that if elected on Oct. 24 they would drop the regional role in housing, economic development, air quality and climate policy, and leave bulk water and sewage treatment for local governments. Daily Hive reports those two utilities already account for most of the regional operating and capital budgets.

Carson Binda, the Conservative candidate for Vancouver-Quilchena, called the present setup “not a utility” but “an unaccountable bureaucratic mess with a blank cheque,” and said Conservatives would “take the chequebook back, focus Metro on water and sewage, and make sure taxpayers get value for every dollar.” The party says consultant and contractor costs now exceed in-house salaries and benefits, cites growing debt and the operating budget, and argues the province and municipalities should take the other four services because that work duplicates what they already do.

Lynne Block, the candidate for North Vancouver-Seymour, said “a smaller, professional board will run this utility like the essential service it is.” The board itself, in July 2026, asked the province to allow a 25 percent cut in directors. Directors now come from 21 municipalities, Electoral Area A and the Tsawwassen First Nation.

On the North Shore Wastewater Treatment Plant, Trevor Withers, the candidate for North Vancouver-Lonsdale, said people “want clean water and working sewers” and not “a regional bureaucracy that can’t build a plant on budget and never answers for it.” Caroline Elliott, the candidate for West Vancouver-Capilano, said Conservatives would audit “what went so disastrously wrong under the NDP’s watch.” Construction began in 2017 at about $700 million, then aimed at 2020. The cost is now about $3.9 billion, with completion in 2030, and households face upward pressure on user fees. The district restarted an independent review this summer, with a final report expected in early 2027. A May 2025 Deloitte review, done with the province, has already led to stronger internal auditing and changes to board pay. In early September 2026 the district parted ways with chief administrative officer Jerry Dobrovolny, in that job since 2019. Civic election day is Oct. 17. Source: [dailyhive.com](https://dailyhive.com/vancouver/bc-conservatives-metro-vancouver-regional-district-reform-platform-promise) https://globalnews.ca/video/12088944/potential-changes-at-metro-vancouver/

# Vancouver Daily News
> **21,824 voters set Vancouver's advance-day record, up 196 per cent from 2022.**

**What You Need to Know:** Vancouver’s first advance-voting day, Saturday, drew 21,824 people and a city record, a 196 per cent increase from the first advance day in 2022. Fifty-nine stations were open, more advance days run this month, and election day is October 17. Elsewhere this morning: a Creston man missing 22 years has been found, a swordfish turned up on Haida Gwaii, and the provincial campaign added a top-end income-tax proposal.

### Top Stories
**Vancouver’s first advance day sets a turnout record: CityNews**
On October 3, Vancouver opened 59 polling stations for the first advanced voting day of the civic election. The City of Vancouver told CityNews by email that about 21,824 people voted, a 196 per cent increase from the first advance day in 2022, and said the city had set a new record for advance voting. Advance voting is also set for October 7, October 10, and October 13, from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. The city said more than 18,000 vote-by-mail packages had been requested, up more than 70 per cent from the 2022 Vancouver election. Election day is October 17. Source: [vancouver.citynews.ca](https://vancouver.citynews.ca/2026/10/04/first-advanced-voting-day/)

**Frank Davis found in the Kootenay River after 22 years: Global BC**
Frank Davis was 40 when he went missing from Creston. For 22 years his disappearance stayed an unanswered mystery for his family. He has been found in the Kootenay River. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12087479/missing-22-years-frank-davis-found-kootenay-river/)

**A swordfish is found on Haida Gwaii: CBC British Columbia**
A swordfish has been found on Haida Gwaii. A University of British Columbia researcher says the finding is unusual, but no longer unexpected, because waters are warming worldwide, including in Canada. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/swordfish-captain-quinn-haida-gwaii-9.7368033?cmp=rss)

### City & Province
**Conservatives field 93 candidates; the NDP is one short: CBC British Columbia**
Elections B.C. says candidate nominations for the provincial election closed at 1 p.m. Saturday, October 3, and that the list is now final. The B.C. Conservatives are running a full slate of 93 candidates. The B.C. NDP is one short, at 92. In Surrey, the Surrey Now-Leader reports a final list of 47 candidates across 10 ridings. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/candidates-finalized-for-bc-snap-election-9.7368782?cmp=rss) https://www.timescolonist.com/2026-bc-votes/bc-conservatives-field-93-candidates-new-democrats-one-short-of-full-slate-12855525, https://surreynowleader.com/2026/10/04/see-the-final-list-of-47-candidates-in-10-surrey-ridings-for-b-c-election/

**Hundreds rally at the legislature over old-growth forests: CBC British Columbia**
Organizers say about 400 people gathered Sunday on the steps of the B.C. Legislature to call for stronger conservation of ancient trees and better forestry practices. Several smaller rallies were held in communities across the province, and organizers say more are planned in the weeks ahead. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/victoria-rally-old-growth-9.7369019?cmp=rss)

### Getting Around
No watches or warnings are in effect for Vancouver. Tomorrow night, DriveBC lists both the eastbound and westbound Dollarton Highway on-ramps closed for paving from 8 p.m. Tuesday, October 6, until 6 a.m. Wednesday, with detours: eastbound via Riverside Drive and Mount Seymour Parkway, westbound via Main Street and Brooksbank Avenue to the Mountain Highway interchange. On Highway 1, traffic is shifted north of the median around 256th Street and crosses back around Lefeuvre Road, with existing eastbound lanes closed, through October 31. In Langley, northbound and southbound traffic on the 264 Street to Highway 13 work is shifted west onto a new bridge through October 17. Environment Canada’s current reading is mainly clear and 11.3 degrees. Monday is mainly cloudy, clearing near noon as morning fog fades, with a high of 16 except 20 inland and a UV index of 3. Monday night falls to 12, with a 30 per cent chance of drizzle after midnight. Tuesday brings a 30 per cent chance of morning drizzle, a high of 16 except 20 inland, and a northwest wind of 30 km/h gusting to 50 late in the morning. Source: [drivebc.ca](https://www.drivebc.ca/) https://weather.gc.ca/rss/weather/49.245_-123.115_e.xml

### Sports
**Golden Knights hold off the Canucks 3-2: NHL.com**
The Vegas Golden Knights beat the Vancouver Canucks 3-2 on Sunday at Rogers Arena. Marc Gatcomb scored the go-ahead goal at 18:28 of the second period, 34 seconds after Jonathan Lekkerimaki had tied it. Paul Cotter scored for Vancouver, his fourth goal in four games, in his 300th NHL game. Kevin Lankinen made 25 saves; Adin Hill made 18. The Canucks are 2-2-0 and the Golden Knights 2-1-0. TSN reports Vancouver is allowing 4.75 goals a game, sixth most in the league, with a penalty kill at 68.8 per cent, and that the Canucks outshot Vegas 9-2 in the third. After the loss, Lankinen said, “I think we’ve got something good cooking here,” and that it is not complete yet. Source: [nhl.com](https://www.nhl.com/news/vegas-golden-knights-vancouver-canucks-game-recap-october-4-2026) https://www.tsn.ca/nhl/article/rebuilding-canucks-see-early-signs-of-growth-weve-got-something-good-cooking-here/

### Both Sides: A higher provincial tax on income over $190,405
What is on the table is a campaign promise, not a tax already in force. On Sunday in Comox, B.C. NDP Leader David Eby said that if the NDP is re-elected, British Columbians earning more than $190,405 a year would pay more provincial income tax, including a new bracket on income over $1 million. Canada’s National Observer reports the election is October 24, and that party documents date the changes to the 2027 tax year.

Eby’s case is that almost everyone would be untouched and the money would go to services. He said more than 96 per cent of residents who make $190,000 or less would see no tax increase, and that the highest earners would pay slightly more “to fund improvements in health care and to lower costs for British Columbians.” He also said it is right to ask people who earn a little more to pitch in when public services are needed. The party said B.C. would be the first large province with a bracket on individuals earning more than a million. The Vancouver Sun reports the proposal would lift the rate above $265,545 from 20.5 per cent to 22.5 per cent, the rate from $190,405 to $265,545 from 16.5 per cent to 18.5 per cent, and set 24.5 per cent on each dollar over $1 million. Eby said the taxes would raise an extra $1 billion a year. National Observer, citing party documents, projects $225 million in 2026/27, $925 million the next year, and $1 billion the year after, and puts the $190,405-to-$265,545 rate at 18.8 per cent.

The Conservative Party of B.C. answers that the plan would tax the doctors and specialists every community is fighting to recruit, while emergency rooms are still closing at night. Its statement said there is no problem the NDP do not think can be fixed by raising taxes, that the party has committed to no new taxes, and that a government led by Lorne Doerkson would make B.C. the place doctors choose to build a practice.

Both sides are responding to a proposal that, as announced, raises provincial tax only on income above $190,405 and only if the NDP is re-elected. Voters go to the polls October 24; NDP documents put any change in the 2027 tax year. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/bc-election-ndp-david-eby-pitches-new-tax-hikes-for-highest-earners) https://www.nationalobserver.com/2026/10/05/news/bcs-eby-promises-new-tax-millionaires-help-pay-health-care
