# Vancouver Daily News
> **Under ninety minutes remain for Vancouver voters before polls close.**

**What You Need to Know:** Vancouver voters are in the last stretch before polls close, with the city promising a count after 8 p.m. Police also have a fresh witness appeal in the CRAB Park homicide, an arrest after a fiery East Side crash, and a new warning about a high-risk offender now living in Vancouver. The Canucks took their first home win of the season.

### Top Stories
**Last chance to vote in Vancouver today: City of Vancouver**
The City of Vancouver says voters still have just under an hour and a half before polls close for the day. The city says to stay tuned for today's count after 8 p.m. A where-to-vote page is posted on the city election site. Source: [vancouver.ca](https://vancouver.ca/election/2026/where-to-vote.aspx)

**Pickup driver arrested after crash into nursing home: CityNews Vancouver**
Vancouver police say a 34-year-old pickup driver is under arrest after a grey GMC Sierra crashed into a nursing home near Renfrew Street and East 22nd Avenue around 1:30 a.m. Friday, then split and burned. The truck had been travelling southbound and struck another vehicle before leaving the road, a witness told police. The driver and a passenger were taken to hospital. Police say no one in the other car or the building was injured. After a hospital assessment he was arrested and faces charges of dangerous operation of a motor vehicle and impaired operation of a motor vehicle. He was served a 90-day driving prohibition, is due in court later, and police have seized the burned truck. The investigation is ongoing. Anyone with information can call the VPD Collision Investigation Unit at 604-717-3012. Source: [vancouver.citynews.ca](https://vancouver.citynews.ca/2026/10/02/truck-crash-flames-vancouver/)

**Police release video in CRAB Park homicide: CBC British Columbia**
The Vancouver Police Department has released surveillance video of two potential witnesses it believes may have information on a homicide in CRAB Park last week. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/police-crab-park-homicide-9.7368197?cmp=rss)

**High-risk sex offender moving to Vancouver, police warn: CTV News**
Police say a sex offender who was the subject of a Surrey warning last month is now moving to Vancouver. The Vancouver Sun reports that Skylar Wayne Pelletier will be monitored by corrections officials and must comply with specific conditions of release. Source: [bc.ctvnews.ca](https://bc.ctvnews.ca/vancouver/article/sex-offender-who-was-subject-of-surrey-warning-last-month-now-moving-to-vancouver-police/) Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/vancouver-police-warn-high-risk-sex-offender-residing-locally)

### City & Province
**Family offers reward in Highway of Tears case: CBC British Columbia**
Tamara Lynn Chipman was 21 when she vanished along Highway 16 in northwestern B.C. in 2005. Her family is offering a $10,000 reward for information. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/indigenous/tamara-chipman-highway-of-tears-9.7365836?cmp=rss)

**B.C. judge names father guardian after child taken to Ukraine: Vancouver Sun**

### Both Sides: AI data centres in Vancouver
Hundreds marched Saturday from Mount Pleasant to downtown against AI data centres, Yahoo News Canada reports. No AI Vancouver called it part of an international day of protest, invited municipal candidates, and said the question is now a campaign issue. The file is a rezoning application for a proposed Mount Pleasant AI data centre. In July, Vancouver city council sent that application back to staff for further public consultation, which will not begin until after the October 17 municipal election.

The case for a pause is put by Torin Larocque, founder of No AI Vancouver, and by four council candidates from COPE, the Vancouver Greens and Bright Future. Larocque says the July referral happened partly because hundreds had signed up to speak, and he wants voters to know which candidates are against AI. COPE's Leslie said the proposal sits in a system that prioritizes the ultra-wealthy over everyone else. COPE's Yi-Kieran said residents do not want the centres, that consultation has been almost absent, and that AI comes up at the door as often as housing and affordability. Both support a moratorium and say the city controls this zoning. Greens candidate Burns wants a moratorium until there is more regulation, but said she does not hear the concern often while door-knocking. Bright Future's Lin said the issue shows a broader need for change in local government. Their stated reasons centre on energy, water and consultation.

Burns's doorstep account and Yi-Kieran's are the two strongest reads in the coverage of how widely people raise it. Council's July vote did not impose a moratorium and did not approve the project. It ordered more consultation after October 17. A 2024 International Energy Agency report cited in the story said data centres, largely driven by AI, used roughly 1.5 per cent of global energy, with that demand projected to more than double by 2030, and with data-centre electricity use growing about four times faster than all other sectors. The fact both the pause advocates and that July order share is that the extra consultation has not started. It is not set to begin before the October 17 vote. ### Both Sides: A cap on staple grocery margins
What is on the table is a campaign promise, not a statute passed this week. At a Kelowna stop on Friday, B.C. NDP Leader David Eby committed to capping profits on some staple products and to steps he said would increase competition. The party billed it as taking the fight to big grocery companies.

Eby's case is that families are paying more while grocery companies' profits rise. He said corporate retailers are using inflation as a cover to raise prices on essential goods, and that "we've all seen our grocery bills go up and up while the profits of grocery giants soar." He singled out Save-On-Foods owner Jimmy Pattison and the Weston family, owners of Loblaws, saying their net worth rose by $4.4 billion in the last year while families struggle. He said not to worry about Save-On-Foods or Jimmy Pattison, who would land on his feet, and that families have to be protected. The price guard, which he compared to a fuel price guard promised the day before, would be a hard ceiling on retail profit margins for milk, cheese, butter and poultry, items that already have wholesale prices managed by marketing boards. The party said that would prohibit unfair markups. He also promised clear per-unit pricing to curb shrinkflation, and a ban on real estate deals and property controls that big chains use to keep smaller stores from opening nearby.

The counterweight in Times Colonist columnist Les Leyne's account is the last grocery promise. Leyne reports the NDP had promised a $1,000 grocery rebate to every family, then abandoned it four months after the election. Asked about that, Eby said his government eliminated the carbon tax, a $2-billion-a-year cut in the tax take. Leyne writes that later price hikes erased a portion of the savings at the pump, after the federal government eliminated the national carbon tax and left B.C. to follow. Both Eby and the column treat rising grocery bills as the problem this promise is aimed at. The commitment was made Friday in Kelowna. Source: [timescolonist.com](https://www.timescolonist.com/opinion/les-leyne-eby-takes-on-grocery-prices-again-12851984)

### Both Sides: Gas tax cuts and price caps at the pumps
Premier David Eby and the B.C. NDP are offering a gas-tax cut and price caps at the pumps if the party is re-elected. Global News reports Eby said the measures would save the average two-car family up to $100 per month and would cost the provincial treasury about $250 million. My Powell River Now reports the same pledge: a gas-tax cut and price caps if the NDP is re-elected. This is a campaign promise. It is not a tax change already on the books.

The case for the pledge, as Eby makes it, starts with the household fuel bill. He said an average two-car family could save up to $100 a month. The Vancouver Sun reports that small business groups welcome the proposal. Their published reason lines up with his: people and businesses who buy fuel would pay less if the tax cut and the caps took effect. That welcome is the strongest non-government case for the pledge in today's coverage.

The case against, in the same Vancouver Sun report, is that at least one economist said the policy will have little impact. The objection does not deny that pump prices matter. It says this design is unlikely to move the price drivers pay by much. Eby is selling a monthly saving. The economist's reported view is that the saving may not arrive.

What both treatments accept is that the tax cut and the caps are a re-election offer, with a treasury cost Eby put at about $250 million, not a completed change at the station. What happens next is the election. Drivers do not get a new pump price from this pledge today. ### Both Sides: The Vancouver Aquatic Centre pool
CBC British Columbia reports that the Vancouver Aquatic Centre may get a 50-metre pool after all, and it links that possibility to the election. The rebuild had plans to build a 25-metre pool. Parties vying for votes are now promising to build a full-sized competition pool as part of the same Vancouver Aquatic Centre rebuild.

The case for the larger pool, as CBC reports it, is that campaign promise: parties seeking votes say they will build a full-sized competition pool, the pool CBC describes as 50 metres, inside the rebuild. That promise is a promise in a campaign, not a pool already approved in the item CBC published.

The case for the shorter pool is the plan already on the project. CBC reports that the rebuild was set to build a 25-metre pool, and it sets the new promises against that plan. The standing design, on CBC’s account, is the 25-metre tank, and the competition-length pool is what those parties are offering to change it to.

The fact both positions share, in that report, is the rebuild itself: the 25-metre plan and the full-sized promise are about the same Vancouver Aquatic Centre project. What is not yet a decision, on CBC’s wording, is the larger pool: the centre “may” get it, and the parties are “promising” it while they vie for votes. ### Both Sides: The drug law and a Vancouver compassion club
A B.C. judge has dropped drug charges against a Vancouver compassion club and ruled the Controlled Drug and Substance Act unconstitutional because it prevents drug users from accessing a safe supply, the Vancouver Sun reports. CBC reports a B.C. Supreme Court judge tossed drug-trafficking convictions against two harm reduction activists who argued they were doing it to reduce the harms caused by toxic drugs.

The strongest case for the club is the one those activists made, as CBC reports it. They argued the point of the supply was to reduce the harms caused by toxic drugs. The Sun's account of the ruling carries that argument to a legal result: the judge found the Act unconstitutional because it blocks drug users from a safe supply.

The strongest case for leaving the statute in place, on the record these reports actually contain, is the court's own pause. The Vancouver Sun says the Supreme Court ruling is put on hold for six months to allow the federal government to change the Controlled Drug and Substance Act. That delay is attributed to the court in the Sun's account. It is the mechanism that keeps the statute available to amend before the judgment takes effect.

What both accounts accept is that operators of a Vancouver compassion club faced drug charges under that federal Act, and that a B.C. court has now ruled for them on safe supply. The next step the Sun names is that six-month window for the federal government to change the Act. **What You Need to Know:** LNG Canada says its Phase 2 expansion in Kitimat is moving forward, a project Ottawa is set to call a historic energy investment and one the company says could double exports from that northern plant. ### Top Stories
**LNG Canada expansion gets go-ahead, as Carney set to highlight 'historic investment' in Canadian energy:** CBC British Columbia

The company says the move could double exports of liquefied natural gas from the northern coastal facility to overseas markets. Prime Minister Carney is set to highlight what is described as a historic investment in Canadian energy. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/carney-lng-canada-announcement-9.7361817?cmp=rss)

**U.S. bans on Canadian booze hit B.C. producers on one of the trade war's thorniest fronts:** CBC British Columbia
As of Tuesday, some Canadian products, including dairy, motorcycles and alcohol, can no longer cross the border into the United States at all, under an American import ban. CBC British Columbia reports that the ban hits B.C. producers. The outlet describes it as the latest escalation in the Canada-U.S. trade war, and says booze has taken centre stage. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/business/us-canadian-booze-ban-whisky-wine-beer-9.7361385?cmp=rss)

**Vancouver transit operator expands into real estate:** The Globe and Mail
TransLink is expanding to become a residential and commercial landlord. In its 2022 investment plan, the agency said it would turn real estate it owns into a revenue source that is not fares and not taxation. The Real Estate Development Program is meant to tighten transit connections and add housing as Metro Vancouver grows. In late July, with PCI Developments, TransLink broke ground on a 31-storey tower at the southwest corner of West Broadway and Arbutus Street in Kitsilano: 256 at-market rental units, 47 below-market rental units, retail space and a public plaza. TransLink chief executive Kevin Quinn and PCI president Tim Grant said the 50/50 partnership came about because the two owned neighbouring properties that would work better as one site. TransLink says it is developing excess land it owns instead of selling it, so it can shape how the buildings are built and how they meet the transit network. The site sits across the street from the future Arbutus Station, the last stop on the Millennium Line extension that is adding six stations along Broadway and linking Burnaby, Port Moody and Coquitlam toward that corridor. PCI's earlier transit hubs include Marine Gateway in Vancouver and the King George Hub in Surrey. Source: [theglobeandmail.com](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/business/industry-news/property-report/article-vancouver-transit-operator-expands-into-real-estate/)

### Both Sides: How West Vancouver luxury homes should be sold
What is being decided, in a market report rather than a council vote, is how homes above $4 million in West Vancouver should be priced and shown this fall. Sotheby's International Realty Canada says the market is firmly in buyers' territory. Its best reason is the count: from Jan. 1 to Aug. 30, 57 properties sold for more than $4 million, a 25 percent decrease from 76 in the same period last year. Managing broker Kevin O'Toole says 195 residential properties were listed above $4 million as of Sept. 1, and that sellers need to be realistic with pricing expectations, conditions and timeframes to attract qualified buyers. The case for a wider net, including a public listing, is also Sotheby's. The firm says its review of land title and MLS records from January 2024 through August 2026 found that one in seven West Vancouver properties above $4 million sells without ever appearing on MLS, and it still says that in current conditions broader public marketing on MLS, with private outreach, is key to attracting qualified purchasers. Chief marketing officer Elaine Hung says that where supply exceeds demand, advisors are encouraging sellers to combine targeted outreach with exposure in premier media and on MLS. Daily Hive, using Zealty, says about 30 homes sold above $4 million in the last 90 days, and that only one of those was ultra-luxury, at $10 million or more. Both readings accept the same drop in sales and the same surplus of listings. The report puts the market in buyers' territory this fall and does not set a date when that would flip. Source: [dailyhive.com](https://dailyhive.com/vancouver/west-vancouver-luxury-real-estate-sept-2026-sothebys)
